parties:
Barat Ali (Md)..Plaintiff-) Respondent------Petitioner 
vs 
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the I Deputy Commissioner, Sirajgonj and others...... Defendant-Appellant------- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1, to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 17-1- 2011 (decree signed on 23-1-2011), pasged by the Joint District Judge (In-Charge), 2nd Court, Sirajgonj, in Other Class Appeal No.78 of 2005,  allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 15-1-2005 (decree signed on 18-1-2005), passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Chowhali, Sirajgonj, in Other Class Suit No.54 of 1999, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that one Md Barat Ali, as plaintiff, filed Other Class Suit No.54 of 1999, before the Senior Assistant Judge, Ullapara, Sirajgonj against the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Sirajgonj and others, being the defendants, with a prayer for declaration of title, in respect of the schedule property. Further case of the plaintiff-petitioner is that, the plaintiff has filed the suit as Secretary of the Pangkharua Graveyard Committee. He further claimed that, 2.59 (two point fifty nine) acres of land were granted pattan/lease by Jaminder Raj Mohani Dashya and others, who have granted the same in CS khatian No. 1 of Mouza Pangkharua, PS Ullapara, District-Sirajgonj.

3. The defendant No. 1 (Government) appeared in this suit and contested by filing written statements denying all material allegation and also claimed that, the suit property was never leased out to the plaintiff and that, the case of the plaintiff is totally false and fabricated.

4. The trial court after hearing the parties, passed the judgment and decree dated 15-1-2005 (decree signed on 18-1-2005) declaring title in the suit property, which has been written in the decree as 2.50 (two point five zero) in CS plot No. 837 corresponding the RS plot No. 1239.

5. Against the said judgment and decree, the defendant preferred Other Class Appeal No.78 of 2005, before the District Judge, Sirajgonj, which was heard by the Joint District Judge (in charge), 2nd Court, Sirajgonj. In appeal the appellate court, after hearing the parties and having considered the evidence on record, allowed the appeal and reversed the findings of the trial court, vide its judgment and decree dated 17-1-2011.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree of the appellate court, the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner filed this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

7. Learned Advocate Mr Md Abdul Hai Sarker appeared on behalf of the petitioner. Having placed the petition alongwith the Materials on record, he mainly submits that, the suit property was recorded in CS kahtain No. 1 of Mouza-Pangkharua, PS Ullapara, District-Pabna, now Sirajgonj and belonged to Jaminder Sothis Chandra and others and they had granted the suit property to the plaintiff for the purpose of using as the graveyard. In support of his contention, he has referred to a piece of paper marked as Ext. 6, whereby, according to his submission, the suit property was granted to one Showkat Ali Mondal, the then President of a committee of the aforesaid graveyard. He also submits that, in the DP khatian No. 580 (Ekhibit 4), it has been recorded that, the suit property has been shown as graveyard, represented by its President Md Barat Ali Mondal (who is the plaintiff). He next submits that, the trial court having seen the aforesaid document of grant granting the lease (Exhibit 6) as well as the DP khatian No. 580 (Exhibit 4) has rightly found that, the plaintiff is the owner and possessor of the suit property. But, the appellate court, while considering the appeal has wrongly assessed the evidence on record and upon wrong findings, it has set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial court. He also submits that, the document of the grant of pattan of lease is unregistered and unstamped. However, the PW 3 Hachen Ali has stated in his deposition that he was present at the time of granting that pattan. Therefore, he submits, the appellate court's finding that, the deed was not a correct deed of pattan was totally based on misreading of evidence and misconception of law and facts. He proceeds on that, the PWs have consistently deposed that, the suit property was never occupied by the Government and the Government had never possessed the same, but the appellate court has totally overlooked the material evidence and thereby committed error of law in its decision and as such, this Rule has merit and the same is liable to be made absolute.

8. Learned Deputy Attorney-General Mr Mohammad Monirul Islam, Mr Sarwar Akhter Masud, AAG and Mrs. Shama Akhtar, AAG have appeared on behalf of the opposite party. The learned DAG having placed the petition and drawing my attention to the paragraph No. 1 as well as schedule to the plaint, first of all submits that, the suit property has been described as 2.50 (two point five zero) acres of land used as graveyard. Therefore, the evidence of the PWs saying that, the suit property is more than one Bigha in the local measurement is beyond the quantity of land (2.50 sfak) as per pleadings and is admissible. He also pointed out that, the trial court did not pass any decree for 2.50 (two point five zero) acres of land. It had passed the decree for 2 (two and half staks. Even then, he also submits, the decree of the trial court is wrong, in view of the clear finding of the appellate court that, the plaintiff did not submit the RS or SA khatain to describe the suit property. Therefore, the trial court's decree, based on RS. Plot No. 1239 without any RS khatain being placed or proved before it, was totally not supported by documentary evidence, while pleadings of the plaintiff is not an evidence. Moreso, the appellate court has examined the certified copy of CS khatain No. 1, which has been marked as Exhibit 1 and found that, the CS Plot No. 1, exhibit 1, was a pond and that CS Plot comprises 2.54 acres of pond with banks, whereas the plaintiff's claim is 2.50 acres of solid land. The learned DAG further submits that, the pond or any water body cannot be granted as pattan for grave-yard. He next submits that, the appellate court has rightly appreciated that, when the nature of the entire suit property even with reference to DP khatain No. 580 (Exhibit 4) is pond (water body with banks), very surprisingly the plaintiff claimed that, he has been using the same as graveyard and possessing the same through cultivation, which is totally absurd. During cross-examination, the DAG points out that, the PW 1 has stated that, there was graveyard in the suit property, which the appellate court has rightly held that, the judgment of the trial court based on mere oral evidence of the PWs without any documentary evidence showing it nature, was totally erroneous and not tenable in the eye of law. He also submits that, the appellate court has rightly assessed the question of lease or pattan of 2.50 decimals of water body or pond to the plaintiff and the same has rightly disbelieved. As regards, the unstamped and unregistered document, purported to be a deed of lease and marked as exhibit 6, the learned law Officers proceeds on that, apparently, this exhibit-6 is a subsequent creation in as much as, the green ink used on this document shows that, the ink has been used recently. Therefore, the appellate court has rightly disbelieved the case of the plaintiff and has rightly set aside the findings of the trial court on this fact. They conclude that in passing the impugned judgment and decree, the appellate court has committed no error of law or facts. The learned DAG submits that, this property is the property of the Government, which the plaintiff has been trying to grab in connivance with the PWs or by gaining over the PWs. The plaintiff, he proceeds on, has apparently abstained from filing the relevant SA and RS khatian for concealing the actual nature and quantity of the suit propert, which is a pond or water body, except for 2½ (two and half) decimals, which has been claimed by the plaintiff, in this plaint, as graveyard granted by the Jaminder. The Jaminder granted 2.50 acres of land (indeed a Fond) for graveyard is not the case of the plaintiff. Therefore, the depositions of PWs are not supported by the pleading and their depositions are apparently false, which, they have given being gained over by the plaintiffs, they submit. He next argue that, in the DP khatain, the nature of the suit property is a pond (exhibit 4), but, the plaintiff has claimed it as a graveyard. If he is Secretary, he ought to have filed the relevant minutes before the trial court. As such he has no locus-standi to file this case. He also submits that, in no circumstances, the plaintiff has been able to prove its case before the court However, in reply to a query made from the Bench, the learned DAG submits that, if there is a graveyard, on 2½ (two and half) decimals of land, then that may be from time in memory the suit property is using as graveyard. The learned DAG concludes that, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court suffers from no illegality or from any other lacuna, whatsoever, and this Rule has no merit and the same may be discharged.

9. I have heard the learned Advocates for both sides, perused the application for revision, lower Court's record as well as the judgment of both the Courts below and other materials in the record.

10. I find that, in the paragraph No. 1 as well as schedule to the plaint, the suit property has been described as 2.50 (two point five zero decimals) of land, claimed to be used as graveyard. Therefore, the evidence of the PWs saying that, the suit property is 2.50 acre is beyond the pleadings and their deposition beyond the cases stated in pleadings is not admissible. The trial court did not pass any decree for 2.50 (two point five zero) acres of land. If the trial court had passed the decree for 2.50 (two and half decimals) of land and the plaintiff accepted it and did not prefer any appeal.

11. The decree of the trial court is not based on evidence, in view of the clear finding of the appellate court that, the plaintiff did not submit the RS or SA khatains to show the nature and quantity of the suit property. Therefore, the trial court's decree, passed in the absence of RS Plot No. 1239 is not at all supported by the documentary evidence, while the statements made in the pleadings of the plaintiff is not evidence.

12. Moreso, the appellate court has examined the certified copy of CS khatain No. 1, which has been marked as Exhibit 1 and found that, the CS Plot No. 1 (exhibit 1) is a pond or water body with banks and that comprises 2.54 acres of land, whereas the plaintiff's claim is 2.50 staks of land only. It also appears that, the pond or water body cannot be granted by way of pattan for using as graveyard. Besides, the nature of the suit property even in the DP khatain No. "580 (Exhibit 4) is pond or water body. This cannot be granted by the Government for using graveyard, nor can be possessed for cultivation by the plaintiff, as stated in the plaint.

13. During cross-examination, the PW 1 has stated that, there was graveyard in the suit property, but the appellate court has rightly held that, the judgment of the trial court based on oral evidence of the PWs, in the absence of the concerned khatians, in which the nature and quantity to the suit property is to be recorded, was totally erroneous and not tenable in the eye of law.

14. The appellate court has rightly disbelieved the question of lease or pattan of 2.50 (two and half) decimals of land to the plaintiff based on a white unstamped and unregistered deed (exhibit 6).

15. This exhibit-6 is a subsequent creation in as much as, the green ink used on this document is apparently of recent origin. Therefore, the appellate court has rightly disbelieved the case of the plaintiff and has rightly set aside the findings of the facts, arrived at by the trial court in passing the impugned judgment and decree.

16. I find that, the suit property belongs to the Government and the plaintiff has been trying to grab the same in connivance with the PWs or by gaining over the PWs.

17. The plaintiff, has apparently abstained from filing the SA and R.S. khatian for concealing the nature of the suit property (a pond with banks).

18. In the DP khatain too, the nature of the suit property is a pond or water body with banks (exhibit 4). The plaintiffs have claimed an water body as a graveyard and that he has been possessing the same by way of cultivation. This is false too.

19. The plaintiffs filed this case as the Secretary of the graveyard committee. But, there is no minutes to show that, he is the Secretary or President or that he was authorized to file this case. Therefore, he has no locus-standi to file this case, which both the courts below have overlooked.

<u>20. In no circumstances, the plaintiff has been able to prove its case before the court below, as has been rightly found by the appellate court. The record of right on the basis of which rent is paid is not a document of title, far less than a DP khatain. So, DP khatain cannot confer any title, which the plaintiff otherwise does not have.</u>

21. When sufficient materials are available on record for disposal of the case, then order for remand of a case is immaterial to help improve the case of the plaintiff. The plaintiff even did not file the SA and RS khatian to identify the nature and quantity of the suit land before this court, to justify a case for remand.

22. However, if the suit property is 2.50 acres or two and half decimals and is being used as graveyard for long time, as has been consistently deposed by all PWs, then the graveyard (more or less than two and half decimals of land) then it should be maintained as graveyard, since the adjacent local users have acquired the vested right in that graveyard, by uninterrupted long use.

23. Therefore, in exercise of the power vested in this Court under Article 112 of the Constitution, the Deputy Commissioner, Sirajgonj, as the proper authority, shall cause to hold a local investigation to ascertain the actual area of the land used as graveyard and shall maintain status-quo in respect of graveyard to the extent mentioned in the schedule of the plaint being 2.50 (two and half decimals) or as may be found after investigation to be made, but in no case below 2.50 decimals (two and half decimals) and shall record the same as the same as graveyard in the khas khatian.

24. In the foregoing discussions, recorded above, I find that, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court suffers from no illegality or from any other lacuna, whatsoever, and this Rule has no merit and the same should be discharged, subject to the direction given herein.

Order

In the result, the Rule is discharged. The impugned judgment and decree dated 17-1-2011 (decree signed on 23-1-2011), passed by the Joint District Judge (In Charge), 2nd Court, Sirajgonj, in Other Class Appeal No.78 of 2005, is hereby upheld, with the direction given hereinabove.

The order of stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.

No costs.

Let a copy of this judgment along with the Lower Court's Record be sent down to the concerned Courts at once.

End.

lawyer:
Mr Nurul Amin, Senior Advocate with Mr. Farid Ahmed, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record.  For the Petitioners 
Mr Abul Kalam Mainuddin, Advocate instructed by Mr Md. Momin Uddin, Advocate-on-Record For Respondent No.6

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 19.02.2017 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2209 of 2014)
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 19.02.2017 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2209 of 2014 discharging the Rule, thereby upholding an order of the Courts below allowing an application for amendment of the plaint and decree passed earlier.

<u>2. The facts relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal are that Khalilur Rahman, father of petitioner No.1 as plaintiff No.5 and Sekandar Ali, father of petitioner No.2 as plaintiff No.6 along with 32 others as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.87 of 1972 before the Court of then Sub Judge No.1, Barishal against 129 defendants for declaration of title over 247.88 decimals of land mentioned in schedule Nos.1-49 by virtue of a settlement and obtained an ex-parte decree on 27.04.1974 and after disposal of the suit, some interested persons tampered with the plaint, schedule, and the ex-parte decree and thereby the suit value and the area of the suit land has been changed. The quantum of the suit land was changed to 1247.88 decimals in place of 247.88 decimals and the suit value was changed to TK. 11,25,000/- in place of 1,25,000/- that is by tampering they added only one digit at the front of the quantum of the suit land and the suit value. The ex-parte decree was challenged by filing a number of miscellaneous cases under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte decree and those were not successful. Therefore, the ex-parte decree dated 27.04.1974 passed in Title Suit No.87 of 1972 is still in force.</u>

3. After knowing the fact, one Abdul Jalil Majhi (third party) and others filed an application before the Court of learned District Judge, Barishal under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure against the said forgery in the plaint and decree of the aforesaid suit. The learned Judge, who after hearing the matter started an inquiry Case No.02 of 1988 and the notice was served upon both parties and after inquiry the learned Subordinate Judge upon hearing all concerned parties and perusing the record, detected the forgery i.e. that in the plaint, suit valuation of the property was shown as TK. 1,25,000/- and the area of the land was shown as 247.88 decimals, and by interpolation, the figure '1’ was inserted at the valuation statement of the suit property as well as the quantum of the land and thereby valuation of the suit property was increased to TK.11,25,000/- and the area of the suit was enhanced to 1247.88 decimals. This forgery was committed in schedule Nos.9, 25, 36, 47 and 48 of the plaint as well as in the ex-parte decree. The Court corrected the same on 27.11.1989 vide order No.88. Against the said order of correction, one Md. Yousuf as a third party filed Civil Revision No.547 of 1990 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which upon hearing was discharged on 13.07.1994. Against the said judgment and order, Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.764 of 1994 was filed before this Division and was dismissed on 02.05.1995, thereby upholding the correction made by the trial Court vide order No.88 dated 27.11.1989.

4. Thereafter, on 16.09.2008, Md. Akkas Ali, respondent-plaintiff No.30 filed an application before the learned Joint District Judge, Court No.02 under Order VI, rule 17 read with sections 151 and 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the plaint as well as the decree of the suit which was allowed on 18.05.2010. The petitioner (son of plaintiff No.5) filed a Civil Revision before the learned District Judge challenging the order dated 18.05.2010 which was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 1. Court, Barishal and was rejected on 06.02.2014. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Additional District Judge, dated 06.02.2014 the petitioner filed Civil Revision No.2209 of 2014 before the High Court Division where the Court affirmed the judgment and order passed by the learned Additional District Judge dated 06.02.2014. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2209 of 2014 dated 19.02.2017, the petitioner filed the instant petition for leave to appeal.

5. Mr. Nurul Amin, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the Court has no jurisdiction to entertain any application for amendment of the plaint after disposal of the suit. In this case, the suit was decreed on 27.04.1974 and the application for amendment of the plaint was allowed on 18.05.2010 and as such, the learned Joint District Judge as well as the High Court Division erred in law in allowing the application for amendment of the plaint. He further submits that after disposal of the suit correction may only be allowed when there is an arithmetical or clerical mistake in the judgment. In the instant case after the initial correction by the learned Subordinate Judge on 27.11.1989, there is no arithmetical or clerical mistake in the judgment. The decree was rightly corrected vide order No.88 passed by the Court on 27.11.1989 deleting the insertions in schedule Nos.9, 25, 47, 48 and 36 which has been upheld by the Appellate Division. But subsequently the learned Sub-ordinate Judge deleted schedule Nos.5, 10, 18, 23, 24, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 37, 38, 43, 44, 45 and 46 vide order No.310 dated 18.05.2010 which is beyond the jurisdiction of the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge). In view of the fact, the learned Joint District Judge as well as the high Court, Division erred in law in allowing the application for amendment of the plaint. Hence the impugned judgment and order dated 19.02.2017 is liable to be set aside.

6. Mr. Abul Kalam Mainuddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.6 submits that the impugned correction has been made on the basis of application before the trial Court under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure upon which an inquiry Case No.02 of 1988 was started and after hearing both the parties the trial Court found prima facie that such gigantic forgery was committed on the record by inserting the figure '1' before the quantum of land and the amount of valuation of the suit in the plaint as well as in the decree. He further submits that the affected person was competent to file that application for deleting the forged portions of the plaint and decree and the forged plaint and decree should not be maintained in the Courts record and in that view of the nature, the Courts below did not commit any illegality.

7. Perusing the leave application, the papers and documents annexed thereto, the relevant provision of law and hearing the learned advocates for both sides, we find that Title Suit No.87 of 1972 was decreed ex-parte on 27.04.1974. A number of miscellaneous cases were filed for the restoration of the suit and setting aside the ex-parte decree and those were not successful. Miscellaneous Case No.92 of 1974 filed for the restoration of original Suit No.87 of 1972 under Order IX, rule 13 was ultimately dismissed and Miscellaneous Case No.94 of 1974 filed under Order IX, rule 13 was also rejected. Thereafter, another Miscellaneous Case No.77 of 1992 for the restoration of the suit was primarily allowed but ultimately was set aside by the appellate Court resulting in the ex-parte decree dated 27.04.1974 passed by the trial Court being upheld by this Division.

<u>8. It appears from the record that the ex-parte decree, after being pronounced, had been interpolated, altering the quantum of land and the value of the suit as well. Subsequently, knowing the fact of forgery, Mr. Abdul Jalil Majhi (third party) and others filed an application for the amendment of the plaint and decree under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 15.11.1989. On the basis of such application for amendment of the decree in the light of finding of enormous forgery by Inquiry Case No.02 of 1988, the Court amended the said decree and plaint on 27.11.1989 vide order No.88 finding that it has been tampered. The matter of correction of forgery in the decree by the trial Court was upheld by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.57 of 1990 and the same has also been upheld by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.764 of 1994. Thereafter, on 11.09.2008, one Akkas Ali, plaintiff No.30 filed another application for amendment of the plaint and decree before the learned Joint District Judge, Court No.2 of Barishal under Order VI, rule 17 read with sections 152 and 151 of the Code on the ground of forgery committed earlier in the ex-parte decree dated 27.04.1974. This application for amendment dated 11.09.2008 so far as it related to the quantum and value of the suit land was allowed by order dated 18.05.2010. That order was upheld by the learned Additional District Judge in Civil Revision No.57 of 2010 by judgment and order dated 06.02.2014. In a further revision filed before the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2209 of 2014 by the impugned judgment and order dated 19.02.2017 the order passed by the Courts below were upheld. Hence, the instant petition for leave to appeal.</u>

9. It appears that the application for amendment which has led to the present petition was filed along with a prayer to delete some schedules from the decree and the suit register. Perusing the inquiry report and orders passed earlier on 27.11.1989 by the lower Court, which has been upheld by this Division in its leave to appeal petition dated 02.05.1995, it is found that only schedule Nos. 9, 25, 47, 48 and 36 had been interpolated and forged and which have been corrected by the Court accordingly by order dated 27.11.1989. The subsequent applications for amendment made on 07.07.2002 and 11.09.2008 under Order VI, rule 17 read with sections 152 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure were not in accordance with the law, since there was no scope to amend the plaint after the decree was passed. So the amendment made by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Barishal vide order No.310 dated 18.05.2010 was not in accordance with the law, since the application incorporated amendment of the plaint, which is not permissible under the law after judgment and decree is signed. It is pertinent to mention that the established principle of law is that once a judgment is delivered by a competent Court and signed by the learned Judge, the said Judge becomes functus officio. He cannot entertain any application other than for correcting an arithmetical or clerical error. It is also well settled that an executing Court cannot go beyond the decree and the executing Court cannot amend the decree without an order passed by the appellate Court, except correction of clerical and arithmetical mistake and an amendment under section 153 of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot be allowed when it alters the real matter in controversy between the parties.

10. In the instant case, the correction made by order dated 27.11.1989 was in accordance with sections 151, 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure. However, in our view the subsequent applications under Order VI, rule 17 read with sections 152 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure were not in accordance with law. Section 152 provides as follows:

"S.152 Clerical or arithmetical mistakes in judgments, decrees or orders or errors arising therein from any accidental slip or omission may at any time be corrected by the Court either of its own motion or on the application of any of the parties."

<u>11. Under this section, the Court may at any time correct any clerical or arithmetical mistake in the judgment, decree or orders or accidental errors arising therefrom either on its own motion or on the application of a party, but an amendment of a substantial nature, or amendment of the plaint is beyond the scope of this section. If the decree or order is sought to be varied for any reason other than clerical error or arithmetical mistake, it can be done only by way of review or by appeal. A Court apart from section 152 by virtue of its inherent power can alter or vary the order and the decree, but the Court must bring the amendment of the decree in conformity with and to harmonies the decree with the judgment. (Ismailullah vs Sukumar, 1986 BLD (AD) 251). But the amendment made by the Court by striking out some schedules from the plaint as well as from the decree was in no way done according to the provision of law. Nonetheless, the Court allowed the petition for amendment of decree vide order No.310 dated 18.05.2010 and as a result it was in violation of the provision of law and the decision of the apex Court. Such order was totally erroneous and the revisional Court's order upholding the same was equally erroneous.</u>

12. Accordingly, having heard the submissions of the learned advocates appearing for the parties concerned, we are of the view that the judgment and order of the High Court Division impugned before us which upheld the erroneous orders passed by the Courts below cannot be sustained.

<u>13. Upon further scrutiny, we are of the view that if the decree and the suit register has not been corrected in accordance with the order dated 27.11.1989, those must be corrected accordingly. That is to say, the decree and the suit register must show the exact and same details in respect of the schedules, plot numbers, quantum of land and value of property as contained in the original plaint before it was tampered/interpolated.</u>

14. Therefore, we direct the trial Court to make the necessary correction of the decree and the suit register so far as it reflects the original plaint and schedules appearing in the original plaint and so far as it reflects the correction made by order dated 27.11.1989 which has been upheld by this Division.

15. In the light of the discussion above, the civil petition for leave to appeal is dis-posed of with the above directions and observations. The judgment and order of the High Court Division as well as those of the lower Courts are hereby set aside.

16. Let the lower Court records be returned immediately.

End.

Thereafter, on 11.09.2008, one Akkas Ali, plaintiff No.30 filed another application for amendment of the plaint and decree before the learned Joint District Judge, Court No.2 of Barishal under Order VI, rule 17 read with sections 152 and 151 of the Code on the ground of forgery committed earlier in the ex-parte decree dated 27.04.1974. This application for amendment dated 11.09.2008 so far as it related to the quantum and value of the suit land was allowed by order dated 18.05.2010. That order was upheld by the learned Additional District Judge in Civil Revision No.57 of 2010 by judgment and order dated 06.02.2014. In a further revision filed before the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2209 of 2014 by the impugned judgment and order dated 19.02.2017 the order passed by the Courts below were upheld. Hence, the instant petition for leave to appeal.

9. It appears that the application for amendment which has led to the present petition was filed along with a prayer to delete some schedules from the decree and the suit register. Perusing the inquiry report and orders passed earlier on 27.11.1989 by the lower Court, which has been upheld by this Division in its leave to appeal petition dated 02.05.1995, it is found that only schedule Nos.9, 25, 47, 48 and 36 had been interpolated and forged and which have been corrected by the Court accordingly by order dated 27.11.1989. The subsequent applications for amendment made on 07.07.2002 and 11.09.2008 under Order VI, rule 17 read with sections 152 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure were not in accordance with the law, since there was no scope to amend the plaint after the decree was passed. So the amendment made by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Barishal vide order No.310 dated 18.05.2010 was not in accordance with the law, since the application incorporated amendment of the plaint, which is not permissible under the law after judgment and decree is signed. It is pertinent to mention that the established principle of law is that once a judgment is delivered by a competent Court and signed by the learned Judge, the said Judge becomes functus officio. He cannot entertain any application other than for correcting an arithmetical or clerical error. It is also well settled that an executing Court cannot go beyond the decree and the executing Court cannot amend the decree without an order passed by the appellate Court, except correction of clerical and arithmetical mistake and an amendment under section 153 of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot be allowed when it alters the real matter in controversy between the parties.

10. In the instant case, the correction made by order dated 27.11.1989 was in accordance with sections 151, 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure. However, in our view the subsequent applications under Order VI, rule 17 read with sections 152 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure were not in accordance with law. Section 152 provides as follows: "S.152 Clerical or arithmetical mistakes in judgments, decrees or orders or errors arising therein from any accidental slip or omission may at any time be corrected by the Court either of its own motion or on the application of any of the parties."

11. Under this section, the Court may at any time correct any clerical or arithmetical mistake in the judgment, decree or orders or accidental errors arising therefrom either on its own motion or on the application of a party, but an amendment of a substantial nature, or amendment of the plaint is beyond the scope of this section. If the decree or order is sought to be varied for any reason other than clerical error or arithmetical mistake, it can be done only by way of review or by appeal. A Court apart from section 152 by virtue of its inherent power can alter or vary the order and the decree, but the Court must bring the amendment of the decree in conformity with and to harmonise the decree with the judgement. (Ismailullah vs Sukumar, 1986 BLD (AD) 251). But the amendment made by the Court by striking out some schedules from the plaint as well as from the decree was in no way done according to the provision of law. Nonetheless, the Court allowed the petition for amendment of decree vide order No.310 dated 18.05.2010 and as a result it was in violation of the provision of law and the decision of the apex Court. Such order was totally erroneous and the revisional Court's order upholding the same was equally erroneous.

12. Accordingly, having heard the submissions of the learned advocates appearing for the parties concerned, we are of the view that the judgment and order of the High Court Division impugned before us which upheld the erroneous orders passed by the Courts below cannot be sustained.

<u>13. Upon further scrutiny, we are of the view that if the decree and the suit register has not been corrected in accordance with the order dated 27.11.1989, those must be corrected accordingly. That is to say, the decree and the suit register must show the exact and same details in respect of the schedules, plot numbers, quantum of land and value of property as contained in the original plaint before it was tampered/interpolated.</u>

<u>14. Therefore, we direct the trial Court to make the necessary correction of the decree and the suit register so far as it reflects the original plaint and schedules appearing in the original plaint and so far as it reflects the correction made by order dated 27.11.1989 which has been upheld by this Division.</u>

<u>15. In the light of the discussion above, the civil petition for leave to appeal is disposed of with the above directions and observations. The judgment and order of the High Court Division as well as those of the lower Courts are hereby set aside.</u>

16. Let the lower Court records be returned immediately.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 25.11.2018, passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3807 of 2015)
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 25.11.2018, passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3807 of 2015, making the Rule absolute with cost of TK.5000/- by which the judgment and order dated 16.09.2015, passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 07 of 2014, has been set aside and the judgment and order dated 30.10.2013 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Savar, Dhaka, in Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013 has been affirmed.

2. Facts leading to filing of this civil Petition for Leave to Appeal, in brief, are:

<u>3. That the predecessor of the present petitioner Nos. 1(a) to 1(d) and 7(a) to 7(b) and petitioner Nos. 2 to 6 and 8 along with one Alekjan Bibi, as plaintiffs, instituted Title Suit No. 121 of 1991 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Savar, Dhaka, for declaration of title in the suit land fully described in the schedule to the plaint.</u>

<u>4. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 filed an application under Order VII Rule 11 of the code of civil Procedure, stating inter alia that the suit has been undervalued showing TK. 25,000/- only whereas the approximate value of the suit land is Tk. 23,00,000/-. Moreover, the plaintiffs did not annex the statement regarding valuation of the suit land to justify the exact value of the suit land and as such, the suit in its present form is not maintainable in law and the plaint should be rejected.</u>

<u>5. The trial Court after hearing the parties rejected the said application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code by Order No. 14, dated 10.05.1992.- Against which, the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule and stay in Civil Revision No. 1247 of 1992. During the pendency of the said Rule, defendant No.2 Kashim Uddin died in 2000 leaving behind the respondent Nos. 1 to 7 as his heirs. -Meanwhile Mr. Abu Sayeed. Ahmed, the learned Advocate who filed the said revision had been elevated to the Bench and as such, it was not possible to substitute the said heirs of the deceased Kasirnuddin (defendant-petitioner No.2 of Civil Revision No. 1247 of 1992)in the said revision. Ultimately, the said Civil Revision stood abated against the opposite parties on 09.07.2008 and as such, the lower Court record was sent back to the trial Court whereupon the proceeding of the suit was re-started and ultimately, the suit was decreed ex parte by judgment and order dated 03.10.2012 against the defendants. Thereafter, on 17.04.2013 the plaintiffs asked the successors of the defendant No.2 to vacate the suit property when they, for the first time, came to know about such ex parte decree. Hence, they filed Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013 under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating inter alia that after arrival of the lower Court record the plain-tiff-respondent Nos. 1 to 7 did not take any step for bringing the legal representatives of the deceased defendant No.2 on record and as such the ex parte decree dated 03.10.2012 would be a nullity as the same has been passed against a dead person.</u>

6. The plaintiffs contested the Miscellaneous case by filing written objection contending inter that the defendant No.2 was not a contesting defendant and as such there was no necessity to substitute his legal heirs in his place and as such the successors of the defendant No.2 have no locus standi to file the application under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code for setting aside the ex parte decree. Thus, there is no ground to interfere with the ex parte decree.

7: The trial Court after hearing the parties allowed the miscellaneous case and set aside the ex parte judgment and decree dated 03.10.2012 and thereby restored the suit to its original file and number by judgment and order dated 30.10.2013. Against which, the plaintiffs preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 7 of 2014 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka which was ultimately heard and allowed by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, by judgment and order dated 16.9.2015 and set aside the judgment and order dated 30.10.2013, passed by the trial Court in Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013.

8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order dated 16.09.2015, the heirs of the defendant No.2 moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 3807 of 2015.

9. The High Court Division upon hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 15.11.2018, upon setting aside the judgment and order dated 16.09.2015 passed by the lower appellate Court and consequently affirming the judgment and order of the trial Court passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013 and thereby restoring the original suit to its file and number and directed the heirs of the defendant No.2 to deposit TK.5,000/- as cost to the Chairman, District Legal Aid Committee, Dhaka within 15 days from the date of receiving the order. In the said order the trial Court was directed to give opportunity to the substituted heirs of defendants to file written statement within a reasonable time and dispose of the suit, in accordance with law, expeditiously, within 1 year from the date of receipt of the order.

10. Hence, the plaintiff petitioners preferred this civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division for redress.

11. Mr. Serajur Rahman, the learned Advocate-On Record, appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the heirs of the late defendant No.2, i.e. the petitioners of Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013 had knowledge of Civil Revision No. 1247 of 1992 from the very beginning and N-10 notice was issued after Mr. Abu Sayeed Ahmed, the learned filing Advocate of the said revision was elevated to the Bench but no step was taken by them for substitution for which the plaintiff petitioners are not responsible, as such the High Court Division and the trial Court failed to appreciate this aspect while passing the judgments. He further submits that the Miscellaneous case was not maintainable and the same is barred by limitation and that they had no locus standi to file the same and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside.

12. Mr. Garib-E-Newaj, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent Nos. 1(a)to 1(c), 2 to 7, 8(a) to 8(f), by filing caveat and supported the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division and submits that the trial Court as well as the High Court Division on consideration of all the materials on record rightly passed the judgment restoring the original suit upon setting aside the ex parte decree as the heirs of the deceased defendants were not aware of re-starting of the suit after being disposal of the Rule by the High Court Division. Hence prayed for dismissal of the civil petition.

13. The points raised herein as to whether the defendant No.2 was a contesting defendant in the suit has already been considered by the High Court Division where-in it found that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 filed application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was rejected by the trial Court by order dated 10.05.1992 against which they filed the earlier Civil Revision No. 1247 of 1992 and during the pendency of the said Rule defendant No.2, Kashimuddin, died in 2000 and in the meantime the learned filing advocate for the said petitioners was also elevated to the Bench and as such the revision was abated due to failure of the petitioners to substitute the heirs of the defendant petitioner No.2. So, it is clear that the defendant no.2 was a contesting defendant in the suit.

<u>14. On the question as to whether the heirs of the defendant No.2 can invoke Order IX Rule 13 of the Code, the High Court Division held that it is the settled principle of law that a defendant against whom an ex parte decree has been passed can either file an appeal against the said ex- parte decree or file an application for review or pray for setting aside the ex parte decree and restoration of the suit under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code or file a fresh suit challenging the ex parte decree. The present respondents being the heirs of deceased defendant No.2 chose to avail the forum of setting aside the ex parte decree and restoration of the suit. Moreover, the said heirs being persons claiming through their predecessor (defendant No.2) can take benefit of section 146 of the Code. Considering which the High Court Division held that the defendant petitioners have a right to file an application under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code and thereby passed the impugned judgment.</u>

15. General principle is the plaintiff is to take steps for substitution of the heirs of any party and since as it appears that the defendant No.2 is a contesting defendant, it was essential for the plaintiff to substitute the said deceased defendant No.2 which the plaintiff appellants did not so. Rather they took the advantage of the death of the said defendant and obtained ex parte judgment and decree against the dead person which is a nullity as has been rightly found by the High Court Division.

<u>16. Thus the findings and decision arrived at by the High Court Division being based on proper appreciation of law and fact the same do not call for any interference by this Division.</u>

<u>17. Accordingly, this civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.</u>

End.

case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 09.11.2014 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.136 of 2013).
full_judgment:
Hassan Foez Siddique J. This appeal No. 448 of 2016 and Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No.804 of 2015 are directed against the Judgment and decree dated 09.011.2014 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 136 of 2013 reversing those dated 20.01.2013 passed by he learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 208 of 2012.

2. The short facts, the disposal of the this appeal and civil petition are that the respondent Nos.1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration of their title alleging that the land respondent No.1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration of their title alleging that the land appertaining to C.S. and S.A. Khatian Nos.23 and 23/2 and plot Nos. 544, 545, 546, 551, 552, 553, 554, 555, 556, 5560, 561, 562, 563, 564, 565, 567, 568, 569, 597, 598 and 599 measuring an area originally belonged to Abdul Samad Munshi, Abdul Jabbar Munshi, Moulavi Abdul Hakim and Kulsum Bibi to the extent of 4 annas shares each under the landlord Ramnarayan Roy Chowdhury and others. By amicable arrangement, Abdul Jabbar Munshi got the land of C.S. Khatian No.23/2, and S.A. Khatian No.9 and plot No.557 measuring an area of 33 acre in his share. He died leaving two sons namely, Md. Shamsuddin and Md. Abdul Gani. The lands of the plots, mentioned above, were acquired in L.A. Case Nos.138/1961-62 but the owners did not get any compensation. The plaintiffs, that is the heirs of Abdul Jabbar Munshi have been Possessing the said land of plot No.557 and in S.A. operation the same was duly recorded I their names. They have dwelling homestead in the said land. On 04.06.2011 the plaintiffs went to pay rent of the suit land to the Government but the defendant No. 4, denied to accept the same claiming that the suit land is the acquitted land of the Government. Knowing about it, the plaintiffs prayed to the authority concerned to get release of the property but in vain. Hence was the suit.

3. The RANK appeared in the suit and filed an application under order VII Rule of the Code of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint stating that the suit is barred by law since the suit land along with other lands were acquired by the Government under section 93A of the Town Improvement Act 1953 the Suit is not maintainable. It is contended that no statutory notice was served upon the RAJUK before filing the suit. Ti is further contended that earlier the plaintiffs filed Writ Petitioner No. 8621 of 2010 for getting release of the said property which was dismissed so the suit is barred by the provision of resjudicata as well.

4. The learned Joint District Judge, rejected the plaint on 20.01.2013. Against which, the plaintiffs preferred First Appeal in the High Court Division and the High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and decree allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of trial court and directed the trial court to proceed with the suit.

5. Thus the Rajuk has preferred civil Appeal No. 448 of 2016 getting leave.

6. On the other hand, Mrs. Shamsunnahar and others filed civil petition for leave to appeal No. 804 of 2015.

7. Since the appeal and aforesaid leave petition have been filed against the same judgment and decree we taken both the matters together for disposal.

8. Mr. Mahbubey Alam learned Senior Counsel papering for the appellant in Civil Appeal No. 448 of 2016, Submits that the suit land was acquired by the Government and the decision of acquisition was duly published in the official gazette in 1965 thereby title and possession of the said land vested with the Government free form all encumbrances, the High Court Division erred in law in entertaining the Suit inasmuch as the same was barred by the provision of law.

9. Mr. Qumrul Haque Siddique, learned Senior Counsel appeared for the plaintiff-respondent in C.A. 448 of 2016. Mr. Siddique submits that the High Court Division upon proper consideration of the materials on record rightly allowed the appeal. He submits that the time of consideration of application under VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure the court shall consider the contents of the plaint only. since there is nothing in the plaint that the suit land was acquire by the Government the High Court Division rightly allowed the plaintiffs to proceed with the case rejecting the application under order VII Rule 11, of the code of Civil procedure. He submits that these plaintiffs have been possession the suit land for about 100 years, the High Court Division rightly rejected the application for rejection of the plaint.

10. On the other hand Mr. A.M. Aminuddin learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner in Civil petitioner for leave to Appeal No. 804 of 2015.

11. Mr. A.M. Aminuddin in his submission adopted the submission of Mr. Mahbubey Alam.

<u>12. The provision of order VII Rule 11(d) of the code of Civil Procedure authorizes the Court to rejects the plaint where the suit appears from the contents of plaint to be barred by any law. In order to decide whether the plaint should be rejected or not, it is necessary for the Court to have a conjoint reading of all paragraphs of the plaint. We have read out all the paragraphs of the Plaint. It appears that the plaintiff in paragraph 5 of the plaint, have stated, “পরবর্তীতে জনস্বর্থে বাংলাদেশ সরকার লালসরাই মৌজার অন্যান্য সম্পত্তিসহ সি, এস, ও এস, এ, ৫৫৭ দাগের সম্পূর্ণ যাহার সি, এস ২৩/২, এস, এ ৯নং খতিয়ানভূক্ত দাগের সম্পূর্ণ ভূমি ১৯৬১-৬২ সালের তৎকালীন পূর্ব পাকিস্তান সরকার নগর উন্নয়ন সংস্থা কর্তৃপক্ষের জন্য অধিগ্রহন করা হইয়াছিল” That is in the plaint the plaintiffs admitted that the property, in question, was acquitted under the provision of 93A of the Town Improvement Act.</u>

13. Mr. Hahbbey Alam, produced photo-state copy of gazette notification published in 25th February, 1965 where it appears that the Government acquired the land of plot No.577 of Mouza Lalasarai, P.S.Tejgaon, District-Dhaka on 18th February1965 under the provision of section 93 A of the Town Improvement Act 1953 along with other lands of the said mouza. At the time of hearing the appeal, the original copy of the said notification was produced before the Court and on perusal of the same, we found that the photo copy produced by Mr. Mahbubey Alam is genuine one.

<u>14. Even where a legal bar against maintainability of a suit is not made out from the contents of plaint but facts showing such a bar are brought to the notice of the Court by the defendant, the court is not powerless to take notice of those facets and give relief to him. Since the property in question has been acquired by the Government and decision of acquisition was published in the official gazette in 1965 the right title and possession of the same vested with the Government free form all encumbrances and the Government, after such acquisition and taking delivery of possession of the same handed over the possession of the same to the then DIT (at present RAJUK). Section 93C of the Town Improvement Act 1953 provides that-</u>

<u>"Except as expressly provided in this Chapter no Civil Court shall entertain any suit or application against any order passed or any action taken under this Chapter and all suites and appeals pending in any such court against any such order passed or any action taken under this Chapter shall abate with effect from the date of coming into force of the Town Improvement (Amendment) Ordinance 1965"</u>

15. In view of the aforesaid provision of law, it is apparent that the instant suit was barred by law. The Provision of order VII rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not exhaustive and the said provision does not limit the inherent power of the court to reject the plaint in a fit case.

16. The learned Joint District Judge, rightly rejected the plaint. The High Court Division erred in law in entertaining the appeal inasmuch as on perusal of plaint it appears that relief claimed therein was barred by the above quoted provision law as such the plaint was liable to be rejected forthwith even without asking the defendant to file his written statement since he plaintiffs admitted in the plaint that the suit land was acquired by the Government. Accordingly, the trial Court did son.

17. Thus we find substance in this appeal. Consequently the appeal is allowed. The judgment and decree of the High Court Division is set aside. The plaint of the instant suit is rejected. The Civil Petition is disposed of in the light of the Judgment and order of the appeal.

End.

parties:
