Vs.
Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Chandpur and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Ismailuddin Sarker J: All these Writ petitions, 13 in number, were heard together as they involve the same point of law and they are being disposed of together by this judgment

2. Writ Petition No.1223 of 1993 was filed by the defendant-judgment-debtors challenging the judgment and decree dated 27-4-93 passed in Artha Rin Suit No.5 of 1992 decreeing the claim of Pubali Bank Ltd. Respondent No.2, for an amount of Taka 1,01,64,101.95 The suit was filed by the Pubali Bank Ltd, a Banking Company, as a financial institution as enumerated in section 2(ka) of the Artha Rin Adalat Act 1990 (Act IV of 1990) for realization of the loan money as enumerated in section 2 (kha) of the said Act.

3. Similarly, in Writ Petition No.601 of 1993 the defendant judgment-debtor challenged the judgment and decree dated 1-12-92 obtained by the respondent-Agrani Bank in Artha Rin Suit No.12 of 1992. Writ Petition Nos.611 of 1993, 612/93, 613/93, 614/93 and 615 of 1993 were filed by the defendant-judgment-debtors challenging the judgments and decrees obtained by the respondent, Pubali Bank Limited, in Artha Rin Adalat Suit Nos.182 of 1990, 183/90, 184/90, 185/90 and 187/90 respectively. Writ Petition No.1518 of 1993 was field by the defendant-judgment-debtors challenging the judgment and decree obtained by the respondent, National Bank Ltd, in Artha Rin Suit No.208 of 1990. Writ Petition No.1123 of 1993 was filed by the defendants-judgment debtors challenging the judgment and decree obtained by the Bangladesh Krishi Bank in Artha Rin Suit No.27 of 1991. Writ Petition No.1589 of 1993 was filed by the defendant-petitioner challenging the judgment and decree dated 27-8-92 obtained by the respondent-Pubali Bank Ltd. in Artha Rin Suit No.253 of 1991. Writ Petition No.1370 of 1993 was filed by the defendant judgment-debtors challenging the judgment and decree obtained by the respondent National Bank Ltd, in Artha Rin Suit No.177 of 1990. Writ Petition No.1406 of 1993 was filed by the defendant-petitioner challenging the judgment and decree obtained by the Bank of Credit and Commerce (Overseas) Ltd. now Eastern Bank Ltd in Title Suit No.219 of 1987 by the Artha Rin Adalat. Writ Petition No.278 of 1993 was filed by the defendant-judgment-debtors challenging the judgment and decree obtained by the Islamic Bank (Bangladesh) Ltd. in Artha Rin Suit No.12 of 1991.

4. The judgments and decrees in all the aforesaid suits were passed by the concerned Artha Rin Adalats and the defendant-judgment-debtors without filing any appeal as provided under section 7 of the said Act have moved this Court by filing the applications under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. In all these applications the petitioners prayed for declaring that the judgments and decrees passed in aforesaid suits be declared as being passed without any lawful authority and of no legal effect. Common grounds taken in all these applications is that the Artha Rin Adalat Act as amended up to date is a void piece of legislation being violative of the provisions of Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution.

5. In the affidavits-in-opposition filed on behalf of the respondent-Banks, the respondents denied that any provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Act is violative of Article 27 or 31 of the Constitution and asserted that the petitioners have equally efficacious remedy by way of appeal as provided by section 7 of the said Act; and the present applications were filed mala-fide in order to delay the realization of the decretal dues from the petitioners.

6. The Artha Rin Adalat Act. 1990 (Act IV of 1990) was passed by the Parliament making special provisions for the purpose of realization of the loan amount advanced by any financial institution. The preamble and long title of the. Act mentioned the purpose of enactment of the Act for recovery of loan advanced by the financial institutions. Section 2(ka) enumerated the financial institutions which have been given the benefit of this Act for recovery of loan as defined in Section 2(kha) of the Act. Section 3 provides that unless there is anything to the contrary in the Act the provisions of the Act are in addition to the provisions of other Acts and will not affect the same. Section 4 provides for establishment of one or more Artha Rin Adalat in the District Head Quarter by investing the Subordinate Judges with the jurisdiction of Artha Rin Adalat. Section 5 provides that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, all suits by the financial institutions shall have to be filed in the Artha Rin Adalat and shall have to be decided by the said Adalat and that the Artha Rin Adalat will function as a civil court and exercise the power and jurisdiction of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure and the provisions of that Code will be applicable to the proceedings of Artha Rin Adalat subject to the provisions of the Act. It further provides that the Artha Rin Adalat shall not grant adjournments for more than 3 times during trial of the suit and shall dispose of the suit within 6 months from the date of filing thereof. Section 5(ka) of the Act provides for publication in the national news paper at the instance of the plaintiff, with the permission of the court, a notice regarding the suit and in case of any doubt about service of summons upon the defendants such notice will be regarded as proof of service of summons of the suit. Section 6(1) provides that subject to the provisions of section 7 no order, judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat shall be called in question before any court or authority. Section 6(2) provides that notwithstanding anything in sub section (1) if the defendant wants to file an application for setting aside an exparte decree under Order IX rule 13 CPC he shall have to deposit at least half of the decretal amount or to furnish a bank guarantee to the extent of the said amount to the trial Court along with the application and unless the same is done the application will not be entertain able. Section 7(1) of the Act provides that any person being aggrieved by any judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat shall have to file appeal within 30 days of the judgment and decree before the High Court Division with the proviso that no appeal shall lie against any ad interim order passed by the said Adalat. Section 7(2) provides that if any defendant desires to prefer an appeal against the order passed in an application under section 6(2) or against the main judgment and decree he will have to deposit half of the remaining decretal amount after deducting the amount already deposited by him, within 30 days, to the High Court Division. Section 7(3) provides that if any defendant desires to file an appeal against the judgment and decree passed by any Artha Rin Adalat he shall have to deposit half of the decretal amount in case no application is filed under section 6 (2) and in case when any application is filed under section 6(2) he shall have to deposit half of the remaining decretal amount after deducting the amount already deposited. Section 7(4) provides that unless deposit of the amount as provided under sub-sections (2)(3) are made by a defendant an appeal by the said defendant shall not be entertain able. Section 8 provides that Artha Rin Adalat shall not allow installments beyond one year to satisfy the decree without consent of the decree-holder with the proviso that in allowing instalments the Adalat shall direct payment of interest at the agreed rate. Section 9 provides that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force any suit by any financial institution pending in any court before the Artha Rin Adalat Amendment Act, 1990 (Act LI of 1990) came into force, shall be transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat of the district in which the court is situated and the provisions of this Act will be applicable to such suits.

<u>7. The common grounds urged by the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the petitioners is that the provisions of section 6 (2) and section 7 of the Act are violative of the fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution inasmuch as section 6(2) requires deposit of half of the decretal amount or bank guarantee to that extent as a condition precedent of filing an application under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside an ex parte decree and section 7 requires deposit of half the decretal amount as a condition precedent of preferring an appeal before the High Court Division within the period of 30 days from the date of the decree whereas Order IX rule 13 and section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure do not impose such condition and limitation for filing an application or preferring an appeal respectively. Borrowers from private persons and institutions other than financial institutions are not required to make such deposit to file an application or prefer an appeal against a decree passed in a money suit. But borrowers from financial institutions have been discriminated against by classifying them together. Such classification of the borrowers of the financial institutions does not rest on a just, fair, reasonable and rational basis and is not sought to achieve the object of the Act and it is discriminatory in nature and as such violated the equality provision of Article 27 of the Constitution. They also urged that Rule of law which is one of the basic structures of the Constitution has also been violated by enacting the said provisions in the Act treating the petitioners differently from other borrowers of private individuals and companies and such discrimination is not permissible. Even there is discrimination between plaintiff and defendant of Artha Rin Adalat suits inasmuchas the plaintiff is not required to deposit any decretal amount for preferring appeal. They also urged that right of appeal is a vested right in the petitioners under section 96 of the Code and that has been taken away from them under the said provision of section 7 of the Act.</u>

8. Learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the respondents, on the other hand, submitted that amongst the same class of borrowers there has not been made any discrimination. All the brorowers of the financial institutions have been grouped together and the rigorous provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Act is equally applicable to all of them. They do not stand on the same footing with the borrowers from private persons and institutions other than the financial institutions. It is also submitted on behalf of the respondents that the financial institutions are not citizens and accordingly no question of violation of fundamental right as enshrined in Article 27 of the Constitution arises and that the classification of the borrowers of financial institution is a reasonable and rational classification for achieving the object of speedy realization of loan advanced to such borrowers by the financial institutions. They also submitted that right to appeal is a creature of the statute and is not vested inherently in a citizen and as such imposing condition for filing an appeal by the statute cannot be objected to.

9. It may be mentioned at the outset that other provisions of the Act have not affected the petitioners in any manner, in filing application under Order IX rule 13 of the Code against ex parte decree or in preferring appeal against exparte or contested decree impugned in these Rules. So we need not consider those provisions.

10. Before considering the vires of section 6(2) and section 7 of the Act let us see what was the object which was sought to be achieved by the Parliament in enacting the Arha Rin Adalat Act including the rigorous provisions of the aforesaid sections The object as stated in the Bill placed before the Parliament is that it is necessary to put an end to existing situation that borrowers of banks and financial institutions are not repaying the loan within time and long time is required to dispose of cases for realization of loan of banks and financial institution under the prevailing law and at times it is not at all possible to realise loan of banks and financial institutions. It also appears from the long title and preamble of the Act that purpose of enacting the Artha Rin Adalat Act 1990 is to make special provisions for realization of loan money advanced by financial institutions which include the banks. So the object of enactment of the Act is to provide for speedy recovery of long pending outstanding loans advanced by the financial institutions to borrowers, most of whom are engaged in trade, commerce and industries for profit making, who developed a culture of non-payment of loan advanced to them as appear from the impugned judgments. So to put to an end to such culture of non-payment of loan by the borrowers of the financial instutions they have been grouped together and special provisions have been made in the Act including rigorous provisions of sections 6(2) and 7 of the Act so that they cannot delay payment of decretal dues for long by filing application under Order IX rule 13 of the Code and/or preferring appeal and staying execution of the decree for a long time without paying at least half of the decretal dues. There is no doubt that the petitioners as borrowers from financial institutions have been put to some difficulties in filing application under Order IX rule 13 of the Code for setting aside ex parte decree and in preferring appeal against the ex parte or contest decree passed by Artha Rin Adalat.

11. We are to see whether classification of the borrowers of financial institutions together in one group from other borrowers of private individuals and institutions other than financial institutions is on just, fair, reasonable and rational basis or unjust, arbitrary and discriminatory and the classification is sought to achieve the object for which the Act has been passed. In other words whether such classification for the purpose of legislation is permissible Petitioners relied on the decision in the case of State of West Bongo vs. Anwar Ali reported in AIR 1952 SC 75. In that case West Bengal Special Courts Act 1950 authorizing the State Government to transfer any criminal case from ordinary criminal court to a Special Tribunal for speedy trial was declared ultra vires of Article 14 of the Constitution of India on the ground that it ignored the principle of classification followed in the Code of Criminal Procedure and it proceeded to lay down a new procedure without making any attempt to particularize or classify the offences or cases to which it is to apply.

12. It may be mentioned that language of Article 27 of the Constitution of Bangladesh is the same as that of Article 5 of the late Constitution of Pakistan 1996 though language of Article 14 of the Constitution of India is a bit different having the same meaning.

13. After the Constitution of Pakistan 1956 came into force provisions of sections 3 and 31 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 providing for compulsory acquisition of rent-receiving interests and payment of compensation at different rates was challenged as violative of the equality provision of Article 5 of the Constitution of Pakistan 1956 in the case or Jibendra Kishore Vs. Province of East Pakistan reported in 9 DLR (SC) 21. The contention was rejected by the Pakistan Supreme Court observing as follows: "Another generalization more frequently stated, is that the guarantee of equal protection of law requires that all persons shall be treated alike under like circumstances and conditions both in the privileges conferred and in the liabilities imposed. In the application of these principles, however it has always been recognized that classification of persons or things is in no way repugnant to the equality doctrine, provided the classification is not arbitrary or capricious, is natural and reasonable and bears a fair and substantial relation to the object of the legislation"

14. Supreme Court of India in the case of DS Nakara vs. Union of India reported in AIR 1983 (SC) 130 while declaring classification of government pensioners merely on the basis of specified date of retirement for payment of increased rate of pension as violate of equality provision of Article 14 of the Constitution of India observed as follows : "Legislative or executive action may accordingly be sustained if it satisfies the twin test of reasonable classification and the rational principle correlated to the object sought to be achieved".

15. Same question arose in the case of Sheikh Abdus Sabur vs. Returning Officer reported in 41 DLR (AD) 30. In that case amended provision of section 7(2)(g) of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance 1983, disqualifying defaulting borrowers of specified banks from seeking election to the office of Chairman or member of Union Parishad, was challenged on the ground that the said provision is violative of the equality provision of Article 27 of the Constitution. Our Appellate Division after reviewing decisions of the USA, India and Pakistan on the question of violation of the equality provision of the Constitution repelled the said contention observing as follows: "Equality before law' is not to be interpreted in its absolute sense to hold that all persons are equal in all respects disregarding different conditions and circumstances in which they are placed or special qualities and characteristics which some of them may posses but which are lacking in others". It was further observed in that case "The legislature while proceeding to make law with certain object in view, which is either to remove some evil or to confer some benefit, has power to make classification on reasonable basis. Classification of persons for the purpose of legislation is different from class legislation, which is forbidden. To stand the test of 'equality' classification besides being based on intelligible differentia must have reasonable nexus with the object legislature intends to achieve by making the classification."

<u>16. In the instant case object of the Act is to put on end to the culture of non-payment of loan advanced to the borrowers of the financial institutions by enacting the special provisions including the provisions of sections 6(2) & 7 of the Act. Petitioners are some of the borrowers of financial institutions and they invested the loan advanced to them in their respective trade, commerce and industry as appear from the impugned judgments. Financial institutions deal with money- deposited with them by private individuals from their savings or by the government from revenue earnings and borrowing from inside and outside the Country. These financial institutions in their turn advance the money deposited with them to borrowers most of whom are engaged in trade, commerce and industries for profit making to further economic activities in the country for greater benefit of the society on condition of repaying the same with interest within the stipulated time. If such borrowers do not pay the loan with interest as per the stipulation in the agreements within time then the financial institutions will face liquidity problem and will not be able to advance loan to new-comers and thus monopolistic tendency will develop in trade, commerce and in Industries depriving new corners the facility of loan from financial institutions. So the defaulting borrowers of the financial institutions have been grouped together and special provisions have been made in the Act to compel them to pay the loan advanced to them. These borrowers are a class by themselves as all of them borrowed money from financial institutions and invested the same in their respective trade, commerce and industry for profit making and developed the culture of non-payment of the same to the detriment of the society at large and for their own benefit only. They do not stand on the same footing with other borrowers from private individuals or institutions other than the financial institutions. They also do not stand on the same footing with the plaintiffs of Artha Rin Adalat suits who are neither citizens nor enjoying the same advantages with the defendants of such suits rather suffering at the hands of such defendants. These defaulting borrowers of financial institutions cannot claim any privilege of continuing with their culture of defaulting repayment of loans and indefinitely withhold the same taking resort to the delatory process of the ordinary civil litigation in the civil court. Classification of these defaulting borrowers into a separate group to compel them to repay the loan advanced to them speedily, in our view, is neither unjust, unfair unreasonable nor discriminatory but necessary in the greater interest of the society. Such classification of the defaulting borrowers of the financial institutions together into a separate group is with the object of removing the evil of the culture of defaulting repayment of loan and for speedy recovery of loan advaryed to them and such object is relevant to the classification. No discrimination has been made as between the defaulting borrowers of the financial institutions in the Act. Thus the said provisions of sections 6(2) and 7 imposing condition in filing application for setting aside ex parte decree or preferring appeal from either ex parte or contested decree have not violated the equality provision of Article 27 of the Constitution as the same satisfies the twin test of reasonable classification and rational principle correlated to the object sought to be achieved. So the decision in the case of Anwar Ali does not help the petitioners. In that case it was also observed that if the legislature takes care to reasonably classify persons for legislative purposes and if it deals equally with all persons belonging to a well defined class, it is not open to the charge of denial of equal protection on the ground that the law does not apply to others also.</u>

17. Rule of law as pronounced by the celebrated English jurist Diecy means not only equality before the law as embodied in Article 27 of our Constitution but also the principle that no man is above the law and the citizens enjoy personal liberty and freedom of thought, expression, association, etc. Since no argument has been advanced except on the question of equality before law which has already been answered it cannot be said that the Act has violated the rule of law or basic structure of the Constitution.

<u>18. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioners that the right of appeal is a vested right and it cannot be taken away by a new law and in support of their contention reliance has been placed in the case of Md. Nazimuddin vs. the State reported in 30 DLR (FB) 49. But on examination of the substituted section 30 of the Special Powers Act regarding appeal it was held that the amending provision is prospective and it did not contain the intention to affect the pending proceedings or right or liability accrued and in that view of the matter it was held that the right to appeal to the High Court Division was vested right. But the Parliament by clear and unambigous language can take away vested right with retrospective effect. Referrence in this respect may be made to the case of Messrs Haider Automobile Ltd. vs. Pakistan reported in 22 DLR (SC) 65.</u>

19. In the instant case section 5 of the Artha Rin Adalat Act provides that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law all suits for realisation of loan advanced by the financial institutions are to be filed in the Artha Rin Adalat and will be decided by such Adalat and section 6 provides that save as provided in section 7 no appeal can be filed and no judgment or decree can be questioned before any other court or authority and section 7 provides for filing of an appeal by the defendant to the High Court Division within 30 days after depositing half of the decretal amount. Section 9 of the Act also provides that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force all the suits for realisation of loan of financial institutions pending in any court before coming into force of the aforesaid amending Act shall be transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat. As such there is clear and unambigous intention of the legislature to take away the vested right of the borrowers of the financial institution to prefer appeal under section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It is now well settled that an appeal is a creature of the statute and unless the statute makes any provision for appeal there is no right of appeal. Reference may be made in this connection to the case of Hari Meah vs. The State reported in 10 DLR 123.

20. Article 31 of the Constitution provides for enjoying protecting of law and to be treated in accordance with law. The Artha Rin Adalat Act 1990 is a law enacted by the Parliament and all borrowers of financial institutions arc treated on the same footing and they are at liberty to take protection of the said law and section 6(2) of the Act enables such barrowers to set aside an ex parte decree and section 7 of the Act provides the right of appeal to such borrowers. So it cannot be said that such borrowers have lost the protection of law or to be treated in accordance with law as enshrined in the said Article 31.

21. A Division Bench of this Court comprising Mr. Justice MA Jalil and Mr. justice Md. Badruzzaman rejected summarily Writ Petition No.289 of 1991 by their judgment dated 30-6-91. In that case the petitioner who was a guarantor for the repayment of a loan taken from respondent No.1, National Bank Ltd. challenged the decree passed in Money Suit No.528 of 1990. The petitioner without filing an appeal filed the writ petition and the same was summarily rejected on the ground that the petitioner had an alternative and efficacious remedy by way of appeal. The petitioner filed Civil petition for Leave to Appeal No. 359 of 1991 and their Lordships of the Appellate Division by the judgment dated 20-7-93 dismissed the leave petition upholding summary rejection by the High Court Division of the writ petition on the ground of alternative remedy provided by law.

22. We have discussed all the provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Act and we do not find any part of the Act to be violative of Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution. Similar view was also taken by another Bench of this court comprising Mr. Justice MA Jalil and Mr. Justice Mohammad Fazlul Karim by their judgment dated 24-11-92 in writ petition Nos.3969, 3971, 3980 and 3981 of 1992 summarily rejecting the writ petitions.

23. In view of the above discussions, we find no merit in the questions raised by the petitioners and accordingly these Rules are discharged with cost and the stay orders granted earlier stand vacated and cost is assessed at Taka 3000.00 (three thousand) in each case.

End.

M Liton Ahmed, Advocate—For the Respondent No.2.

full_judgment:
Md Zakir Hossain, J: At the instance of the petitioners, the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order No. 56 dated 21-1-2019 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2015 by the Artha Rin Adalat, 4th Court, Dhaka (Annexure-I) in rejecting the said Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2015 preferred under section 19(2) read with section 57 to the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, this Court was further pleased to direct the parties to maintain status quo in respect of transferring and/or disturbing the peaceful possession of the petitioners over the mortgage properties as mentioned in the schedule to the Writ Petition, for a period of 1(one) month which was subsequently extended from time to time by this Court. 

3. Facts leading to the issuance of this Rule may be stated, in brief, as follows: 
The respondent No. 2, Southeast Bank Limited, Principal Branch, Motijheel instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 39 of 2012 before the Artha Rin Adalat, 4th Court, Dhaka, hereinafter shortly referred to the Adalat, for realization of outstanding dues to the tune of Taka 3,73,76,433.91 against the petitioners. No summons was served upon the petitioners; therefore, the petitioners could not contest the suit. But the plaintiff-Bank, by practicing fraud upon the Adalat showing appearance of defendant-petitioners in the suit, submitted successive adjournment petitions for filing written statement. Ultimately, on 22-11-2012, the Artha Rin Suit No. 39 of 2012 was decreed ex-parte and thereafter, the decree was drawn up on 27-11-2012. After that, the respondent-Bank put the decree into execution by filing Artha Rin Execution Case No. 13 of 2013. 

4. During the pendency of the execution case, the Adalat was pleased to issue a certificate of ownership in favour of the Bank. The petitioners were not at all aware as to the ex-parte decree. When the Bank officials refrained from supplying specific information regarding the outstanding loan amount on different pleas, on 23-8-2015, the petitioners came to know the fact that the Bank obtained an ex-parte decree against the petitioners. Thereafter, the petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2015 under section 19(2) read with section 57 to the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, hereinafter shortly referred to the Ain, 2003. 

5. Having received the notice of the Miscellaneous Case, the respondent-Bank filed written objection. Thereafter, the Miscellaneous Case was fixed for final hearing. After that, the petitioner No. 2 was examined as PW-1 and accordingly, his deposition was recorded in part. During the pendency of the hearing, the petitioners filed an application for seeking opinion of the Hand Writing Expert to compare with the signatures and writings of vakalatnama with those of adjournment petitions and vakalatnama alleged to have been filed by the defendant-petitioners in the Artha Rin Suit. 

6. Upon hearing the parties, the Adalat was pleased to allow the said application seeking the opinion of the hand writing expert. Accordingly, the petitioners deposited the fees of hand writing expert on the very date. Surprisingly, on 01-11-2018, the respondent-Bank filed an application under section 19(5) read with section 57 of the Ain, 2003 for rejection of the Miscellaneous Case. The petitioners contested the said application by filing written objection. Upon hearing, the Adalat was pleased to reject the Miscellaneous Case holding the view that the petitioners failed to deposit 10% of the decretal amount within the prescribed time and thereafter, on the basis of the petition of the respondent-Bank under section 33(7Ka) read with section 57 of the Ain, 2003, the Adalat was pleased to reject the Miscellaneous Case and issued process for delivery of possession of the properties as mentioned in the schedule Nos. IV and V of the Writ Petition. Challenging the legality and propriety of the rejection order of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case, the petitioners were constrained to move this Court and obtained the Rule and status quo thereto. 

7. The learned Senior Advocate Mr MA Samad along with Mr Mohammad Mehdi Hasan, Mr Mohammad Mazharul Islam and Mr Md Manjurul Basit appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that being conversant to the fact of ex-parte decree the petitioners filed the Miscellaneous Case under section 19(2) read with section 57 of the Ain, 2003 within 30 days from the date of knowledge with a promissory note on 16-9-2015 and later on, the petitioners deposited pay order on 21-6-2016 amounting to Taka 37,37,643.40 i.e. 10% of the decretal amount, which was accepted by the Adalat and eventually, the Miscellaneous Case was fixed for peremptory hearing, but the Adalat without concluding the hearing most illegally and arbitrarily rejected the Miscellaneous Case. Relying on the decision of the case of Bangladesh Development Bank Ltd vs Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore, reported in 66 DLR 1, he next submits that section 19(2) of the Ain, 2003 clearly contemplates two different situations for filing an application to set-aside the ex-parte decree and for the restoration of the suit in its original file and number. One is right after passing of the ex-parte decree and other one is from the date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree as the case may be, and when the question of knowledge is the basis for deciding an application for setting aside the ex-parte decree, it should be decided in a proper Miscellaneous Case upon taking evidence and hearing the parties. But unfortunately, the Adalat without examining the materials on record most illegally rejected the Miscellaneous Case. He further submits that fraud vitiates everything and as the fraud is very much apparent in the Artha Rin Suit as to the issuance and service of summons, the Adalat ought to have allowed the Miscellaneous Case. He also submits that the impugned ex-parte decree is liable to be turned down to do substantive justice by this Court and hence, the entire proceeding of the Execution Case is liable to be quashed as its foundation is based on fraudulent ex-parte decree. 

8. Mr Samad further submits that no summons was issued and served upon the defendant-petitioners in the Artha Rin Suit and the respondent-Bank by filing vakalatnama and adjournment petitions on behalf of the defendant-petitioners showing their appearance, managed to obtain an ex-parte decree fraudulently and collusively, which would be crystal clear on perusal of the order sheets of the Artha Rin Suit and other materials on record. 

9. He next submits that decree passed without proper service of summons is a nullity and it is imperative upon the Court to knock down the decree to secure the end of justice. In support of his submissions, he relies on the ratio of the cases Government of Bangladesh vs Mashiur Rahman, reported in 50 DLR (AD) 205 and Sonali Bank Ltd. vs Prime Global Ltd., reported in 63 DLR (AD) 99. 

10. As against to this, Mr M Liton Ahmed appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 2, Bank, submits that the arguments advanced by the Advocates of the petitioners are fallacious and not tenable in the eyes of law. Finally, he submits that in order to prolong the litigation, the petitioners filed this Writ Petition; therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

11. Now the pertinent issues are—
i. Whether the ex-parte decree dated 22-11-2012 was obtained by practicing fraud apparent on the record of the Artha Rin Suit No. 39 of 2012, 
ii. Whether summons was duly served upon the defendant-petitioners, 
iii. Whether the Execution Case No. 13 of 2013 arising out of the ex-parte decree passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 39 of 2012 is liable to be quashed, 
iv. Whether the impugned order is legally sustainable in the eyes of law. 

12. We have perused the writ petitions along with annexures and affidavit-in-opposition, arguments advanced by the parties and legal position intricately involved in this case with great care and attention and seriousness as it deserves. 

13. Having received the plaint, the Adalat registered Artha Rin Suit No. 39 of 2012 by its order No. 1 dated 9-4-2012, which may be stated hereunder as verbatim for better appreciation and understanding:

“রেজিষ্টিভুক্ত করা হউক। ইহা টাকা আদায়ের মোকদ্দমা । মোকদ্দমার তায়দাদ মং ৩,৭৩,৭৬,৪৩৩/৯১ টাকা। বাদী পক্ষ ফিরিস্তি দ্বারা ফটোকপি/মুল কাগজপত্র দাখিল করিয়াছে। নথিভুক্ত রাখা হউক বাদীপক্ষ কোর্ট ফি দাখির করে নাই । তলবনামা দাখিল করিয়াছে । বাদীপক্ষ কোর্ট ফি দাখিলের জন্য সময়ের আবেদন করিয়াছে । আবেদন মঞ্জুর করা গেল। আগামী ২৪-৪-১২ইং তারিখ কোর্ট ফি দাখিল ও প্রয়োজনীয় আদেশের জন্য রহিল ।”
Order No. 2, dated 24-4-2012 may be read thus:

“অদ্য কোর্ট ফি দাখিলের জন্য দিন ধার্য আছে। বাদীপক্ষ কোর্ট ফি দাখিলের জন্য এক দরখাস্তের মাধ্যমে সময় প্রার্থনা করেছেন। প্রার্থনা মঞ্জুর করা হল। আগামী ৩০-৪-১২খিঃ তারিখ কোর্ট ফি দাখিল ।”
Order No. 3, dated 30-4-2012 runs as follows:

“বাদী পক্ষ ৫০,০০০ টাকা বক্রী কোর্ট ফি চালানের মূল কপি সহ দাখিল করিয়াছে। সেরেস্তারের প্রতিবেদন দেখিলাম । কোর্ট ফি সহ মোকদ্দমাটি সাময়িকভাবে গ্রহণ করা হইল । নেজারত যোগে ও রেজিঃ ডাকযোগে বিবাদী পক্ষের প্রতি সমন ইস্যু করা হউক । আগামী ১৫-৫-১২ইং তারিখ সমন ও এডি ফেরত ।”
Order No. 4, dated 15-5-2012 may be read thus:

14. By order No. 11, dated 22-11-2012 the Adalat on the basis of the plaint filed with affidavit passed ex-parte decree, the operative portion is as follows: 

“এ মোকদ্দমাটি বিবাদীদের বিরুদ্ধে একতরফা সূত্রে খরচা সহ ৭-৪-১২খ্রিঃ পর্যন্ত ৩,৭৩,৭৬,৪৩৩/৯১ (তিন কোটি তেয়াস্তর লক্ষ ছিয়াত্তর হাজার চারশত তেত্রিশ টাকা একানব্বই পয়সা) টাকার ডিক্রী হলো। ৮-৪-১২গ্রিঃ তারিখ থেকে টাকা আদায় হওয়া পর্যন্ত বাদীপক্ষ অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন, ২০০৩ এর ৫০(২) ধারায় বর্ণিত সুদসহ প্রাপ্ত হবে। বিবাদীপক্ষকে রায় প্রচারের ৬০(ষাট) দিবসের মধ্যে ডিক্রীকৃত টাকা সুদসহ বাদী পক্ষের অনুকূলে পরিশোধের নির্দেশ দেওয়া হইলো। ব্যর্থতায় বাদী পক্ষ আদালতযোগে আইন এবং পদ্ধতি মোতাবেক ডিক্রীকৃত টাকা আদায় করে নিতে পারবে । মোকদ্দমা দীয়েরের পরবর্তীতে বিবাদীপক্ষ কোন টাকা জমা প্রদান করলে বাদীপক্ষকে উক্ত টাকা বাদ দিয়ে পরবর্তী কার্যক্রম গ্রহণ করার জন্য নিদের্শ দেয়া হলো ।”

15. Challenging the legality of the status quo order passed by this Court at the time of issuance of the Rule, the respondent-Bank filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 636 of 2019. In the CPLA, the respondents i.e. the petitioners of the instant Writ Petition filed paper book and additional paper book. After considering the materials on record and submissions of the learned Advocates, the Appellate Division was pleased to dismiss the CPLA No. 636 of 2019 on merit. 

16. Section 7 of the Ain, 2003 deals with the provisions regarding service of summons. The provisions are not exhaustive, therefore, it has to be read with the provisions so far it relates to service of summons as laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in short the CPC, and the Civil Rules and Orders, in short the CRO. In this respect, the provisions of section 7 of the Ain, 2003 may be read as follows: 

৭। সমন জারী সম্পর্কিত বিধান।—(১)আপাততঃ বলবৎ অন্য কোন আইনে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, বাদী আদালতের জারীকারক কর্তৃক এবং প্রাপ্তি স্বীকারসহ রেজিস্ট্রীকৃত ডাকযোগে প্রেরণের নিমিত্ত, আরজির সহিত সমন জারীর জন্য সমুদয় তলবানা আদালতে দাখিল করিবেন, এবং আদালত অবিলম্বে উহাদের একযোগে জারীর ব্যবস্থা করিবেন, এবং যদি সমন ইস্যুর ১৫ (পনের) দিবসের মধ্যে জারী হইয়া ফেরত না আসে, অথবা তৎপূর্বেই বিনা জারীতে ফেরত  আসে, তাহা হইলে আদালত উহার পরবর্তী ১৫ (পনের) দিবসের মধ্যে বাদীর খরচায় ষে কোন একটি বহুল প্রচারিত বাংলা জাতীয় দৈনিক পত্রিকায়, এবং তদুপরি একটি স্থানীয় পত্রিকায় যদি থাকে, এবং আদালত যদি ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থে প্রয়োজনীয় মনে করে, বিজ্ঞাপন প্রকাশের মাধ্যমে সমন জারী করাইবেন, এবং অনুরূপ জারী আইনানুগ জারী নামে গণ্য হইবে।
(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এর বিধান এর অতিরিক্ত হিসাবে বাদী যদি নিজ খরচায় কোন সমন ও নোটিশ বিবাদীর উপর জারী করাইতে ইচ্ছা করেন, তাহা হইলে আদালত পূর্ববর্তী উপ-ধারায় আদালতের জারীকারক কর্তৃক সমন জারীকরণের প্রথমোক্ত ব্যবস্থাটির অতিরিক্ত এই ব্যবস্থাটিও কার্যকর করিবে ।
(৩) জাতীয় দৈনিক পত্রিকায় বিজ্ঞাপন প্রকাশের মাধ্যমে সমন জারীর আগাম ব্যবস্থা হিসাবে বাদী আরজি দাখিলের সময় আদালতে আরজির সহিত একটি নমুনা বিজ্ঞাপন দাখিল করিবেন, এবং আদালত পূর্ববর্তী উপ-ধারার বিধান অনুযায়ী করণীয় হইলে, উক্ত বিজ্ঞাপনটি -প্রয়োজনীয় সংশোধন বা পরিবর্তন সাপেক্ষে, তাৎক্ষণিকভাবে জারীকরণের নিমিত্ত প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা করিবেন। 

17. Let us examine the provision of section19 of the Ain, 2003, which may be read thus: 

 “১৯।একতরফা ডিক্রী সম্পর্কিত বিধান। —(১)মামলার শুনানীর জন্য ধার্য কোন তারিখে বিবাদী আদালতে অনুপস্থিত থাকিলে, কিংবা মামলা শুনানীর জন্য গৃহীত হইবার পর ডাকিয়া বিবাদীকে উপস্থিত পাওয়া না গেলে, আদালত মামলা একতরফা সূত্রে নিষ্পত্তি করিবে।
(২) কোন মামলা একতরফা সূত্রে ডিক্রী হইলে, বিবাদী উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রীর তারিখের অথবা উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রী সম্পর্কে অবগত হইবার ৩০ (ত্রিশ) দিবসের মধ্যে, উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রী রদের জন্য দরখাস্ত করিতে পারিবেন।
(৩) উপ-ধারা (২) এর বিধান অনুযায়ী দরখাস্ত দাখিলের ক্ষেত্রে বিবাদীকে উক্ত দরখাস্ত দাখিলের তারিখের পরবর্তী ১৫ (পনের) দিবসের মধ্যে ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের ১০% এর সমপরিমান টাকা বাদীর দাবীর সেই পরিমাণের জন্য স্বীকৃতিস্বরূপ নগদ সংশ্লিষ্ট আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানে, অথবা জামানতস্বরুপ ব্যাংক ড্রাফট, পে-অর্ডার বা অন্য কোন প্রকার নগদায়নযোগ্য বিনিমেয় দলিল (Negotiable Instrument) আকারে জামানত হিসাবে আদালতে জমাদান করিতে হইবে ।
(৪) উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধানমতে ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের ১০% এর সমপরিমাণ টাকা জমাদানের সংগে সংগে দরখাস্তটি মঞ্জুর হইবে, একতরফা ডিক্রী রদ হইবে এবং মূল মামলা উহার পূর্বের নম্বর ও নথিতে পুনরুজ্জীবিত হইবে, এবং আদালত এ মর্মে একটি আদেশ লিপিবদ্ধ করিবে; এবং অতঃপর মামলাটি যে পর্যায়ে এক তরফা নিষ্পত্তি হইয়াছিল, এ পর্যায়ের অব্যবহিত পূর্ববর্তী পর্যায় হইতে পরিচালিত হইবে ।
(৫) বিবাদী উপ-ধারা (৩) বিধানমতে ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের ১০% এর সমপরিমাণ টাকা বাদীর দাবীর সেই পরিমাণের জন্য স্বীকৃতিস্বরূপ নগদ সংশ্লিষ্ট আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানে, অথবা জামানতন্বরূপ ব্যাংক ড্রাফট, পে-অর্ডার বা অন্য কোন প্রকার নগদায়নযোগ্য বিনিময়ে দলিল (Negotiable Instrument) আকারে জামানত হিসেবে আদালতে জমাদান করিতে ব্যর্থ হইলে, উক্ত দরখাস্তটি সরাসরি খারিজ হইবে; এবং আদালত ঐ মর্মে একটি আদেশ লিপিবদ্ধ করিবে ।
(৬) অর্থ খণ আদালতে বিচারাধীন কোন মামলা, বাদীর অনুপস্থিতির বা ব্যর্থতা হেতু খারিজ করা যাইবে না, এবং এইরূপ ক্ষেত্রে আদালত, নথিতে উপস্থাপিত কাগজাদি পরীক্ষা করিয়া গুণাগুণ বিশ্লেষণে মামলা নিষ্পত্তি করিবে ।” 

18. Section 57 of the Ain, 2003 provides inherent or instinct power of the Court, which may be read as follows: 
৫৭। আদালতের সহজাত ক্ষমতা।–এই আইনের অধীন অভিপ্রেত ন্যায় বিচারের উদ্দেশ্য সাধনকল্পে অথবা আদালতের কার্যক্রমের অপব্যবহার রোধকল্লে প্রয়োজনীয় যে কোন পরিপূরক আদেশ প্রদানে হইয়াছে বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে না।”

19. Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 provides: 
Nothing in this Code shall be deemed to limit or otherwise affect the inherent power of the Court to make such orders as may be necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the Court. 

20. The inherent power of the Court should be exercised at its discretion according to the merit of each case. This discretionary power should not be exercised when restoration of the original suit will negate the interest of justice. 

21. In this respect, .the ratio set out within the bounds of the judgment pronounced in the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Mashiur Rahman, reported in 50 DLR (AD) 205 may be stated as under: 
"It is a cardinal principle of administration of justice that no result of any judicial proceeding should be allowed to receive judicial approval from any court of law whenever it is obtained by practising fraud upon the court; reason being fraud demolishes the very foundation of sanctity of such judicial proceeding. It is also well established principle of law that fraud vitiates all judicial proceeding. Thus contravention of the provision of law, cannot be a valid ground for allowing an order obtained by fraud to stand. When the trial court itself on consideration of the materials on record was satisfied that a fraud had been committed in obtaining the ex-parte decree it was the duty of the trial court to set-aside the ex-parte decree. The failure of the trial court in the performance of its legal obligations ought not to have been maintained by the High Court Division in affirming the finding of the trial court." 

22. The ratio of the judgment pronounced by Appellate Division in the case of Sonali Bank Ltd. vs Prime Global Ltd., reported in 63 DLR (AD) 99 may be profitable for a better appreciation and understanding of the submission of the learned Advocate of the petitioners. In this case it was held that—
"15. The irresistible conclusion from the above facts is that the decree, so far the defendant No. 2 is concerned, was passed without any service of summons upon it or even without any attempt to do so. As such, it is a nullity in the eye of law and it is imperative upon any Court of law, which is in seisin of the matter, to hold so, even without invoking the provisions of section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain or rule 13 of Order IX of the Code of Civil Procedure. Because rule 13 envisages at least a service, even if not `duly' and sub-section (1) of section 19 also envisages a service of summons upon the defendant. In the instant matter, however, these provisions need not to be invoked when there is a total absence of any kind of service or attempt to do so upon the concerned defendants." 

23. In the case of Md Refat Ali vs Govt. of Bangladesh, reported in 2001 BLD (HCD) 133, the Government filed a miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 13 for setting aside an ex-parte decree on the ground that summons was not served upon the Deputy Commissioner or to any authorized officer. After filing of the case, an application under section 151 of the Code was filed to set-aside the ex-parte decree alleging that no summons was at all issued. This application was opposed mainly on the ground that, once the Government filed a case under Order IX rule 13, no relief could be given under section 151. On scrutiny of the record, it was found that,, summons was not at all issued upon the Government and thereafter the Court set-aside the ex party decree on the ground that it was obtained by practicing fraud upon the Court. In this respect, the relevant paragraph of the said judgment may be stated thus: 
"It is true, ordinarily the court does not exercise its inherent power under section 151 of the Code of Civil procedure whenever a remedy is available to the aggrieved party under any provision of the Code of Civil Procedure. But it is also well-settled that if the disputed Order or decree is obtained by a party by practicing fraud upon the Court or it is has been occasioned due to the fault of the Court or Court officials, the Court has not only the competence in exercise of its inherent power under section 151 of the Code to undo the wrong done to the aggrieved party but also it is imperative in the interest of justice to do so fraud always vitiates all solemn transactions and a fraudulent act by its own nature is a nullity in the eye of law and it is never protected by law. In such cases, it will be highly inequitable and in just to ask the wronged party to seek his relief under other arduous and time consuming provisions of law instead of giving him a relief under section 151 of the Code as the special preserve of the Court for doing justice. It deserves to be noted in this connection that procedures are just means towards advancement of the cause of justice and not certainly for obstructing it in the name of technical fall-outs. The filing of an application under Order 9, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot be allowed to stand in the way of the relief the defrauded defendant is entitled to under the Law. We are satisfied in the facts of the case, that the learned Subordinate Judge rightly exercised his power under section 151 of the Code in giving the appropriate relief..." 

24. In the case of Ram Chandra Singh vs Savitri Devi, (2003 ) 8 SCC 319, para-15, it was held that—
"Commission of fraud on court and suppression of material facts are the core issues involved in these matters. Fraud as is well-known vitiates every solemn act. Fraud and justice never dwells together." 

25. In the case of Bangladesh Development Bank Ltd. vs Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore and others, reported in 66 DLR 1, it was held: 
"12. Two aspects have been made abundantly clear in the said provisions of law that an application for restoration of the suit after setting-aside ex-parte decree may be made within 30 days right after passing of the ex-parte' decree or from the date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree. The words and phrases in sub-section 2 of section 1.9 of Ain "একতরফা ডিক্রির তারিখের অথবা উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রি সম্পর্কে অবগত হইবার..." clearly contemplate two different situations for filing an application for restoration. One right after passing of the ex-parte decree and the other one from the date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree as the case may be. The word `অথবা' in the said provision made the two situations disjunctive..." 

26. In the case of Jahangir Kabir Chowdhury vs Bangladesh Government, 22 BLC (AD) 139, it was held: 
"There is no doubt that this power can be exercised sparingly—it is a power to promote justice and prevent abuse of the process of the court but if the Adalat finds that by practicing fraud or by false representation, a party has obtained a judgment or order, the Adalat can always interfere..." 

27. On close perusal of the applications for filing written statement dated 14-6-2012 and 16-7-2012, along with the applications for time to file Court-fees dated 9-4-2012 & 24-4-2012 and application for adjournment of ex-parte hearing file by the plaintiff on 13-9-2012 & 26-9-2012, it is as clear as daylight that the writings of those applications are similar and written by the same person. It is also crystal clear that the same person filled up both the vakalatnamas and adjournment petitions for the plaintiff and defendants. 

28. On perusal of the writings of the aforesaid applications and vakalatnamas in a very naked eyes, anybody or even a layman can come to the conclusion that the writings therein have similarity and they have been done by the same person and therefore, it can safely be concluded that by practicing a flagrant fraud upon the Adalat and the defendant-petitioners, the ex-parte decree was obtained by the plaintiff-respondent Bank. 

29. Apart from the same, on meaningful reading and meticulous perusal of the order-sheets as depicted above it also transpires that with an ulterior motive, the plaintiff-Bank or its appointed a lawyer or lawyer's clerk may inconnivance with the Court-staff showed the appearance of the defendants in the Artha Rin Suit to secure ex-parte decree on the spur of the moment. Moreover, it is admitted by the Executing Court that no copy of summons or Postal AD is on the record. The order-sheet does not show that talabana was filed by the plaintiff to issue summons upon the defendants as per the mandate of section 7 of the Ain, 2003. The Executing Court itself held the view that the petitioner-defendants raised the allegation of fraud but unfortunately, the Executing Court did not take trouble to look into the record wherein it can easily be seen that fraud is apparent. Hence, we unequivocally hold the view that fraud and justice cannot stand together. 

30. It further transpires that in fact, no talabana was submitted by the plaintiff and accordingly, no summons was issued and served upon the defendant-petitioners in accordance with law, therefore, the ex-parte decree is a nullity i.e. void ab initio. It also transpires that by practicing fraud upon the Adalat the plaintiff-Bank managed to fix a date for ex-parte hearing and without adducing any evidence by a mechanical process, the plaintiff obtained the ex-parte decree and thereby, infringed the long established principle of audi alteram partem. Therefore, the ex-parte decree cannot stand in the eyes of law and it is liable to be knocked down. In the Miscellaneous Case, the petitioners deposited 10% of the decretal amount which was accepted by the Adalat and the decree-holder prayed for withdrawing the same, therefore, the Executing Court cannot hold the view that the requirement of section 19(5) of the Ain, 2003 has not been complied with. Where ex-parte decree is contaminated due to apparent fraud, the petitioners do not require paying 10% of the decretal amount. In an appropriate case, the Adalat may invoke section 57 of the Ain, 2003 to do justice and to undo injustice. The Adalat could have set-aside the ex-parte decree invoking section 57 of the Ain, 2003 as it was obtained by practicing fraud apparent on the record. 

31. To find out the perpetrators who committed fraud, the Adalat shall hold inquiry in accordance with law. Let us look into the relevant provisions of sections 476 and 195 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, in short the CrPC, which may be read as follows: 
"476. (1)—When any Civil, Revenue or Criminal Court is, whether on application made to it in this behalf or otherwise, of opinion that it is expedient in the interests of justice that an inquiry should be made into any offence referred to in section 195, sub-section (1), clause (b) or clause (c), which appears to have been committed in or in relation to a proceeding in that Court, such Court may, after such preliminary inquiry, if any, as Court, such Court may, after such preliminary inquiry, if any, as it thinks necessary, record a finding to that effect and make a complaint thereof in writing signed by the presiding officer of the Court, and shall forward the same to a Magistrate of the first class having jurisdiction, and may take sufficient security for the appearance of the accused before such Magistrate or if the alleged offence is non-bailable may, if it thinks necessary so to do, send the accused in custody to such Magistrate, and may bind over any person to appear and give evidence before such Magistrate: 
Provided that, where the Court making the complaint is High Court Division, the complaint may be signed by such officer of the Court as the Court may appoint. 
For the purpose of this sub-section, a Metropolitan Magistrate shall be deemed to be a Magistrate of the first class  
(2) ……………….  
(3) ……………….  
"195. (1) No Court shall take cognizance: 
(a) ……………….  
(b) ……………….  
(c) of any offence described in section 463 or punishable under section 471, section 475 or section 476 of the same Code, when such offence is alleged to have been committed by a party to any proceeding in any Court in respect of a document produced or given in evidence in such proceeding, except on the complaint in writing of such Court, or of some other Court to which such Court is subordinate. 
(2) In clauses (b) and (c) of sub-section (1), the term "Court" includes a Civil, Revenue or Criminal Court, but does not include a Registrar or Sub-Registrar under the Registration Act, 1908  
(3) ……………….   
(4) ……………….   
(5) ……………….   

32. Now in this respect, we have come to the decision that fraud was committed in obtaining ex-parte decree, but who are real perpetrators cannot be determined at this stage. The Artha Rin Adalat is a special Court having the trappings of a civil Court. The Adalat is not powerless to hold inquiry to find out the perpetrators who committed forgery. In this respect, the learned Judge of the Adalat following the procedures laid down under section 476 of the CrPC shall hold inquiry by himself and after holding inquiry as per the mandate of section 476 of the CrPC, if it is possible to identify the perpetrators, the Adalat shall make a complaint to the concerned Magistrate having jurisdiction to take cognizance under section 195(1)(c) of the CrPC. 

33. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that the Rule has got merit and accordingly, the Rule is legally bound to be made absolute. As the ex-parte decree has been tainted with apparent fraud and nullity due to lack of service of summons, the execution proceeding shall certainly be collapsed. If a foundation of a building is not strongly laid down, obviously, the super-structure shall collapse. As the ex-parte decree is not well founded as per law, therefore, the entire execution proceedings shall fall through. 

34. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, however, without passing any order as to costs. Accordingly, the ex-parte decree dated 22-11-2012 passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 39 of 2012 is hereby set-aside and the Artha Rin Suit No. 39 of 2012 be restored in its original file and number. Thus the Artha Rin Execution Case No. 13 of 2013 is quashed and hence, the Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2015 be disposed of. 

35. The earlier order of status quo granted by this Court stands vacated and recalled. 

36. Having received the copy of the judgment, the Adalat shall fix a date for submitting written statement not exceeding 15 days. After filling the written statement, the Adalat will proceed in accordance with the Ain, 2003. It is further directed that the Adalat shall dispose of the Artha Rin Suit with outmost expedition preferably within 06(six) months from the date of reception the copy of the judgment. No adjournment petition shall be entertained from either side. The Adalat is also directed to hold inquiry under section 476 of the CrPC by registering a separate Miscellaneous Non-judicial Proceeding to find out the perpetrators who committed forgery in the proceeding of Artha Rin Suit No. 39 of 2012 and if the perpetrators are identified, then the Adalat shall make a petition of complaint to the concerned Magistrate under section 195(1)(c) of the CrPC having jurisdiction to take cognizance of the offence. The Adalat may keep the original vakalatnamas and adjournment petitions as stated earlier in a safe custody so that those documents cannot be destroyed by anybody. 

Let a copy of the judgment be communicated to the Court below at once. 

End.
