parties:
Mohid Uddin (Md) -------- Defendant-Appellant-Petitioner
vs
Kamrun Nahar ---------- Plaintiff-Respondent-Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Md Rezaul Hasan, J: This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 13-7-2017, passed by the Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet, in Family Appeal No.48 of 2016, affirming the judgment and decree dated 21-6-2016 (decree signed on 30-6-2016), passed by the Assistant Judge, Bianibazar & Family Court, Sylhet, in Family Suit No.14 of 2015, decreeing the suit should not be modified and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, the High Court Division has directed the petitioner to deposit 50% of the amount of Taka 7,33,000 (seven lac and thirty three thousand): Learned Advocate Mr M Moshiur Rahman has appeared for the petitioner. He submits that, the petitioner has deposited 50% of the amount at Taka 7,33,000 (seven lac and thirty three thousand) as per direction given by the High Court Division at the time of issuance of the Rule on 26-11-2017. 

3. Facts, relevant for disposal of this Rule, in brief are that, one Kamrun Nahar, as plaintiff, had filed a Family Suit No.14 of 2015, before the Court of Assistant Judge, Bianibazar and Family Court, Sylhet, against Md Mohid Uddin (husband of plaintiff), seeking dissolution of the marriage between them as well as praying for the dower money amounting to Taka 14,93,700 (fourteen lac ninety three thousand and seven hundred) and maintenance of the plaintiff at the rate of Taka 20,000 (twenty thousand) per month, from 3-2-2012 alongwith the maintenance of the infant, at the rate of Taka 5,000 (five thousand) per month, from 18-9-2012. I have perused the averments made in the plaint, which has not been repeated here. The defendant had contested in the suit by filing a written statement, in which he had denied all material allegations and further stating his positive case described in pragraph-5 of the written statement. The plaintiff herself had testified as PW 1. The plaintiff had also proved and filed certain documents, marked as Exhibits-1 and 2, respectively. On the other hand, the defendant has examined himself as DW 1 and had also produced DW 2 (Abul Kalam), to support the defence case. 

4. The Trial Court, after hearing the parties and having assessed the evidence on record, had decreed the suit on 21-6-2016 (decree signed on 30-6-2016). 

5. Being aggrieved thereby, the defendant has preferred Family Appeal No.48 of 2016, which was heard by the Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet, and the appellate court has dismissed the same and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court in Family Suit No. 14 of 2015. 

6. Being dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the appellate court, the defendant-appellant has filed this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the instant Rule. 

7. Learned Advocate M Moshiur Rahman has appeared for the defendant-appellant-petitioner, as noted herein before. He has challenged the calculation of amount payable to the plaintiff-respondent-opposite party. He submits that, at the time of pronouncement of the judgment passed by the trial court on 21-6-2016, the age of infant was 45 months, but the trial court had awarded Taka 2,08,000 as maintenance for 52 (fifty two) months, instead of 45 (forty five) months and thereby, on the date of judgment, the trial court has allowed 7 (seven) months excess maintenance for the infant, at the rate of Taka 4,000 (four thousand) per month, which comes at Taka 28,000. He further submits that, the appellate court as the last court of fact, did not correct this mistake. He concluded submitting that, the finding of the appellate court is liable to be set-aside and the judgment and decree may be modified in accordance with law. He prays that, the Rule has merit and the same may be made absolute. 

8. Learned Advocates Mr MA Jabber has appeared for the plaintiff-respondent-opposite party. He frankly conceded that, in passing the judgment and decree, the trial court had allowed an excess amount of Taka 28,000 (twenty eight thousand) i.e. for 7 months maintenance of the minor infant (7 x 4,000). The learned Advocate has submitted a supplementary-affidavit on 22-11-2020, in which he has calculated the amount as per the judgment and decree of the trial court and as upheld by the appellate court, however, by adjusting Taka 28,000 (twenty eight thousand) paid in excess as maintenance to the infant, at the time of passing the judgment and decree by the trial court. He has next drawn my attention to the paragraph-9 of the supplementary-affidavit and submits that, after adjustment of the aforesaid 28,000 (twenty eight thousand), a total amount of Taka 6,34,500 becomes payable as decreetal debt. The learned Advocate next drawn my attention to the documentary and oral evidence on record, and further submits that, the plaintiff has proved her case by consistent and adequate oral and documentary evidence. He also submits that, although the defendant had testified as DW 1 and produced another person as DW 2, but the defendant could not establish the defense case with reference to the evidence given by them, while the defendant has failed to produce any appropriate documentary evidence. He further submits that, although the defendant had claimed in his pleading to have sent some amount of money through postal money order, as maintenance of the plaintiff, however, the defendant was not able to produce or to prove any money order or any other documents before the court below in support of his claim about payment of maintenance to the plaintiff or to the infant.. He also submits that, the conduct of the defendant has proved that, he is not a credible person. The learned Advocate next submits that, the trial court has discussed all necessary issues in view of the documentary and oral evidence on record and found that, the plaintiff has been able to prove her case and had decreed the suit. The learned Advocate also submits that, the appellate court, as 'a last court of fact, and has discussed all evidence on record as well as the points for determination, and the appellate court has concurred with the findings of the trial court and has rightly dismissed the appeal. The learned Advocate concludes submitting that, the petitioner has no case and the court below has rightly passed the impugned judgments and decree and that the court below has committed no error of law, nor that has resulted in any error in the decision given, nor the impugned decision has occasioned in failure of justice. Therefore, the Rule has no merit and the same may be discharged with exemplary cost. 

9. I have heard the learned Advocates for the petitioner and for the opposite party, perused the revisional application alongwith the judgment of the courts below, the Supplementary Affidavit (filed on 22-11-2020) and the evidence on record, as maintained in the LCR. 

10. I find that, the marriage between the parties is an admitted fact and it is also admitted that, there was an infant, born out of the wedlock of the parties. I also find that, this suit for dissolution of marriage alongwith claim for dower money and the maintenance of the plaintiff and of the infant has been decreed by the trial court, vide it judgment and decree dated 21-6-2016 (decree signed on 30-6-2016). 

11. I also find that, the trial court has discussed all evidence on record and has rightly decided all the issues infavour of the plaintiff, having arrived at the correct findings, except a minor calculation mistake as regards the maintenance of the infant, as noted herein before. I also find that, the appellate court had dismissed the appeal on contest and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

12. Having discussed the present revisional application, supplementary-affidavit (filed on 22-11-2020), judgment and decree alongwith the evidence on record, I do not find any misreading or non reading of any evidence and the courts below have arrived at correct findings. 

13. I also find that, in passing the impugned judgment and decree the appellate court has committed no error of law and that same has not resulted in any error in the decision, nor has occasioned in failure of justice. Rather the defendant had tried to linger this matter, since 2016 till now. 

14. Besides, I find that, there is an allegation that, the defendant has falsely described himself as a lawyer. But, I do not find any Sanad (certificate) produced by the defendant before the courts below, to prove that he is an advocate. 

15. I have also found that, the plaintiff (wife) had conceived and she was sent to her father's house. But there is no evidence on record to show that during this time, the defendant had given any maintenance through any money order or otherwise to the plaintiff as alleged by the defendant. 

16. There is no documentary evidence on record to show that, the defendant has paid any cost of delivery of their child or for medical treatment when the plaintiff was pregnant, nor he has paid any amount of money for her operation purpose, since a scissor operation was required. Therefore, apparently, all these cost and expenses were borne by the plaintiff's father, since he had no other option but to do everything within his means to save the live of his daughter and that of the in fact, all though these costs are to be paid and borne by the husband (defendant). 

17. It should be made clear that, maintenance, in such a case as the present one, is not confined only to the costs of providing foods and clothings, it should also include the costs of boarding or shelter (if incurred), the entire cost required for the medical treatment, for doing surgery, for buying medicine and the costs of health and care of the mother, the embryo, the fetus and the new born, in all cases where such cost or any of these are proved to have been incurred by the plaintiff (wife) or her guardian or well wishers or that might be found remaining as debt on her or on her guardian or well wisher, as the case may. 

18. I find a serious allegation that, the defendant tried to persuade the plaintiff (the wife) to kill the embryo. 

19. It should be noted here that, at pragraph-9 of the supplementary-affidavit dated 22-11-2020, the plaintiff has made a calculation of her claim as per judgment and decree of the court below, by adjusting Taka 28,000 (twenty eight thousand) paid in excess. Now, in total Taka 6,34,500 (six lac thirty four thousand and five hundred) is payable. 

20. The plaintiff has waived her claim incurred on other accounts, as mentioned in preceding paragraph, hence these are kept out of consideration, in this particular care. The defendant should pay to the plaintiff the said amount of Taka 6,34,500 (six lac thirty four thousand and five hundred) within 60 (sixty) working days, from the date of receiving the copies of the judgment and order by the court concerned, failing which the defendant shall pay penal interest on the said amount till realization of the judgment debts in full. 

21. Before, parting of, it should be noted here that, the moment High Court Division passes any judgment and order, it becomes the law of the land in view of the provisions of Article 111 of the Constitution, unless the same is modified/set-aside or operation of the same is stayed by the Appellate Division 'Ref: Government of Bangladesh vs Md Mosharraf Hossain, 64 DLR (AD) 21). This decision is binding upon the all subordinate courts as regards the ambit and entitlement of the right to maintenance. 

22. In view of the forgoing discussion, I find no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree. This Rule has no merit 
Order 
Accordingly, the Rule is discharged with appropriate direction. The impugned judgment and decree dated 13-7-2017, passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet, in Family Appeal No.48 of 2016, affirming the judgment and decree dated 21-6-2016 (decree signed on 30-6-2016), passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Bianibazar and Family Court, Sylhet, in Family Suit No.14 of 2015 is hereby up held. 
The defendant is directed to pay to the plaintiff Taka 6,34,500 (six lac thirty four thousand and five hundred only) within 60 (sixty) working days, at a time or in four equal installments, from the date of receiving copy of this judgment and order alongwith the LCR by the concerned trial court, failing which the petitioner shall remain liable to pay penal interest on the said amount, at the rate of Taka 200 (two hundred) per day, to the plaintiff till realization of the judgment debt, in full, which shall be recovered through the Family Execution Case No. 9 of 2016, pending before the Court of Assistant Judge, Bianibazar, Sylhet, by attaching and selling the assets of the defendant, and/or by attaching the proceeds in his bank account (if any) and directing the bank to pay the said amount (not exceeding the decreetal debt) to the plaintiff, through court, or by directing his employer and/or the creditor to pay the same to the plaintiff (through court), for which, if required, a garnishee order may be passed and/or by detaining him in civil prison and or by seizing his passport (if any) and prohibiting his leaving the country, by passing appropriate order on the immigration authority. 

The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby stand vacated. 

Send down the copy of the Judgment and decree alongwith LCR records at once. 

End.

Zakir Hossain (Md) -------- Petitioner
VS
Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Zakir Hossain, J: At the instance of the petitioner, the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the Respondent Nos. 1-3 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree vide (Annexure-H and H-1) passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 96 of 2011 of the Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka passed by the respondent No.1 shall not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect as the same have been passed without considering the defendants-petitioner's application dated 15-11-2012 for rejecting the statements of accounts marked as Exhibit No. 12 as per order No. 34 dated 7-7-2013 vide (Annexure-F) and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. At the time of the issuance of the Rule, this Court was pleased to stay the operation of all further proceedings of Artha Jari Case No. 2 of 2014 pending before the Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka for a period of 6(six) months which was subsequently extended from time to time by this Court. 

3. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule are, in brief, as follows: 
The Respondent No.3, Dhaka Bank Limited being plaintiff filed Artha Rin Suit No. 96 of 2011 before the Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka, hereinafter shortly referred to 'the Adalat' for realization of outstanding dues to the tune of Tk. 59,49,103.93. The defendant entered appearance in the suit and by filing written statement denied the material allegations set out in the plaint contending inter alia that the suit is not constituted as per the requirements of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, hereinafter shortly referred to the Ain, 2003. After conclusion of the trial, the suit was decreed on contest. It is stated in the writ petition that the statement of accounts was not certified in view of the provision of section 2(8) and section 4 of the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 nevertheless, it was marked as Exhibit-12 with objection and thereafter, the petitioner filed an application to expunge the Exhibit-12 as it was not duly certified. The Adalat disposed of the petitioner's application dated 7-7-2007 holding the view that at the time of pronouncement of judgment it will be considered but without considering the same, the Adalat passed the impugned judgment and decree against the petitioner, therefore, the same is liable to be set-aside. Challenging the legality and propriety of the judgment and decree of the aforesaid Artha Rin Suit No. 96 of 2011, the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the aforesaid Rule and stay therewith. 

4. Mr AKM Asiful Haque the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the statements of accounts admitted as evidence (Exhibit-12) did not comply with the requirements of section 2(8) and section 4 of the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891, therefore, the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat cannot stand on its leg and it is liable to be set-aside by this Court. 

5. He further submits that though the Adalat in its order dated 7-7-2007 stated that the objection as to the admissibility of the Exhibit-12 be considered at the time of pronouncement of judgment but unfortunately, the Adalat did not consider the Exhibit-12 and, as such, the Adalat committed an error of law causing serious failure of justice. 

6. Finally, he submits that since the Adalat decreed the suit on the basis of inadmissible evidence, therefore, the decree is liable to be turned down, otherwise it will entail serious injury to the petitioner. 

7. As against to this, the learned Advocate Mr ASM Abdur Razzaque appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 submits that the writ petition is not at all maintainable in view of the well settled principle enunciated by the Appellate Division that the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Suit cannot be challenged by way of writ petition. He also submits that the petitioner deliberately avoided alternative and efficacious remedy as available in the Ain, 2003 and filed this writ petition which is ex facie illegal and therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged. In support of his contention, he refers to the case of Zahirul Islam vs National Bank Limited, reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191 and Gazi M Towfic vs Agrani Bank, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6. He finally submits that the writ Court has got no jurisdiction to entertain the merit of the case therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

8. He further submits that the statements of accounts have been rightly admitted as evidence in view of the special rules of evidence as embodied in the Ain, 2003. 

9. The pertinent issues of this case are—
i. Whether the writ petition is at all maintainable in the eye of law; 
ii. Whether the statement of accounts (Exhibit-12) marked by the Artha Rin Adalat is legally admissible as evidence. 

10. We have perused the entire materials on record, the affidavit-in-opposition, the writ petition along with the annexures and legal position involves in this case with great care and attention and seriousness as it deserves. 

11. In order to answer the issue No. 1, we should consider some ratio enunciated by the Appellate Division in different cases. 

12. In the case of Zahirul Islam vs National Bank Limited, reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, where it has been decided as follows: 
"The petitioner, without filing any appeal, filed an application under Article 102 of the Constitution, namely, Writ Petition No. 892 of 1991, which was dismissed summarily by a Division Bench of the High Court Division on 30-6-1991 on the ground that the petitioner has an alternative and efficacious remedy by way of appeal... The Petition is dismissed." 

13. In the case of Gazi M Towfic vs Agrani Bank, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6 their Lordship of the Appellate Division clearly spelt out to the effect—
"...the law is now settled that since special provision for appeal has been made against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat no application under Article 102 lies against such judgment and decree..." 

14. In the case of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) vs Artha Rin Adalat, reported in 59 DLR (AD) 6 the Appellate Division held: 
"...there being specific remedy in the statute for filing appeal against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat in the present case the defendant not availing of the aforesaid remedy cannot maintain writ petitions..." 

15. The Judgment-debtor has alternative remedy to prefer Appeal against the decree under section 41 of the Ain, 2003 but by flouting the said provision, he filed this Writ Petition which is not maintainable in the eye of law. As the petitioner did not challenge the legality and propriety of the decree in view of the aforesaid provision of the Ain, 2003, the decree, has acquired finality. The law is settled now that no petition under the Article 102(2) of the constitution lies impugning the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in a case filed by Financial Institution for realization of loan amount. 

16. In order to answer the issue No. 2, we should go into the relevant provisions as enshrined in the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891. 
Section 2(8) and section 4 of the said Act may be read as follows: Section 2(8)—"Certified copy" means a copy of any entry in the books of a bank together with a certificate written at the foot of such copy that it is a true copy of such entry, that such entry is contained in one of the ordinary books of the bank and was made in the usual and ordinary course of business, and that such book is still in the custody of the bank, such certificate being dated and subscribed by the principal accountant or manager of the bank with his name and official title. 
Section 4—Subject to the provisions of this Act, a certified copy of any entry in a banker's book shall in all legal proceedings be received as prima facie evidence of the existence of such entry, and shall be admitted as evidence of the matters, transactions and accounts therein recorded in every case where, and to the same extent as, the original entry itself is now by law admissible, but not further or otherwise. 

17. In the case of Radheshyam G Garg vs Safiyabai Ibrahim Lightwalla, reported in AIR (1988) Born. 361, it was held: 
"In my judgment the aforesaid view of the learned Judge of the lower appellate Court was hypertechnical. The said extract of account was duly signed by the Agent of the bank. Implicit in it was a certificate that it was a true copy of an entry contained in one of the ordinary books of the bank and was made in the usual and ordinary course of business and that such book was in the custody of the bank. The detailed ingredients mentioned in the defining Clause 8 of Section 2 of the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 for qualifying to be 'certified copy' are not mandatory but merely directory. Sufficient compliance depending upon facts and circumstances of each case is enough to qualify a document to be 'certified copy'. I, therefore, hold that the said extract of account produced at Exh. 55. A is admissible in evidence..." 

18. The Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is a special law which is clearly conceived from its preamble, objects and reasons as appended to the Draft Bill presented to the Parliament by the concerned Ministry. Section 8 of the Ain, 2003 has clearly stated that the essential ingredients to be incorporated in the plaint, as plaint is the foundation of the plaintiff's case. 
Section 8 of the AM, 2003 may be read as follows—
“৮। আরজি।–(১) অর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান আরজি দাখিলের মাধ্যমে মামলা দায়ের করিবে এবং উক্ত আরজিতে, অন্যান্য বিষয়ের মধ্যে, নিম্নবর্ণিত বিষয়সমূহ উল্লিখিত হইবে, যথাঃ-
………..
(২) পূর্ববর্তী উপ-ধারায় বর্ণিত বিষয়াদির অতিরিক্ত, বাদী, আর্জিতে আরও অন্তর্ভুক্ত করিবে-
(ক) একটি তফসিল, যাহাতে প্রদর্শিত হইবে-
(অ) বিবাদীকে প্রদত্ত মূল খণ বা, ক্ষেত্রমত, বিনিয়োগকৃত টাকার পরিমাণ;
(আ) স্বাভাবিক সুদ বা ক্ষেত্রমত, সুনাফা বা ভাড়া হিসেবে আরোপিত টাকার পরিমাণ;
(ই) দণ্ড সুদ হিসাবে আরোপিত টাকার পরিমাণ;
(ঈ) আর অন্যান্য বিষয় বাবদ বিবাদীর উপর আরোপিত টাকার পরিমাণ,
(উ) মামলা দায়েরের পূর্ব পর্যন্ত প্রণীত শেষ হিসাব মতে বিবাদী কর্তৃক বাদী আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানকে ঋণ বা পাওনা পরিশোধ বাবদে জমাদানকৃত টাকার পরিমাণ; এবং
(ঊ) বাদী কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ও ধার্য মোট এবং বিবাদী কর্তৃক পরিশোধিত মোট টাকার তুলনামূলক অবস্থান..”

19. The relevant provisions of sections 6(2),
(3) and (4) of the Ain, 2003 may be stated for better appreciation.
Section 6(2) of the Ain, 2003 may be read as follows—
৬। বিচার পদ্ধতি ।__(২) এই আইনের অধীন কোন মামলা আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক আরজি দাখিলের মাধ্যমে দায়ের করিতে হইবে, আরজির বক্তব্য এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট দালিলিক প্রমাণাদির সমর্থনে আরজির সহিত একটি হলফনামা (Affidavit) সংযুক্ত করিতে হইবে, আরজির সহিত প্রদেয় কোর্ট ফি (ad valorem) প্রদান করিতে হইবে এবং দাখিলকৃত আরজি যথাযথ হইলে আদালতের নির্ধারিত রেজিস্টারে উহা ক্রম অনুসারে অন্তর্ভুক্ত করিতে হইবে।

Section 6(3) of the Ain, 2003 runs as follows—
৬। বিচার পদ্ধতি।—(৩) এই আইনের অধীন লিখিত জবাব দাখিলের মাধ্যমে প্রতিদ্বন্ধিতা করা যাইবে, লিখিত জবাবের বক্তব্যের এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট দালিলিক প্রমাণাদির সমর্থনে লিখিত জবাবের সহিত একটি হলফনামা (Affidavit)সংযুক্ত করিতে হইবে এবং দাখিলকৃত লিখিত জবাব মামলার নথিতে সামিল হইবে।
Section 6(4) of the Ain, 2003 may be read as follows—
৬। বিচার পদ্ধতি ।--(৪) এই আইনের অধীন অর্থ ঋণ আদালতে মামলা নিষ্পত্তির ক্ষেত্রে উপ-ধারা (২) ও (৩)এর বিধান অনুযায়ী সংযুক্ত হলফনামা (Affidavit) মৌলিক সাক্ষ্য(Substantive evidence) হিসাবে গণ্য হইবে, এবং আদালত কোন মামলার একতরফ। বা তাৎক্ষণিক নিষ্পত্তির ক্ষেত্রে কোন সাক্ষীকে পরীক্ষা ব্যতিরেকে, কেবল এইরূপ হলফনামা-যুক্ত আরজি বা লিখিত জবাব ও সংশ্লিষ্ট দালিলিক প্রমাণাদি বিশ্লেষণ করিয়া রায় বা আদেশ প্রদান করিবে ।

20. Section 6(4) clearly spelt out that the affidavit filed by the petitioner along with the plaint and written statement shall be treated as substantive evidence and even without taking evidence, the court may pronounce its judgment on perusal of the plaint and written statement. On plain reading of the plaint, it transpires that the plaint was filed fulfilling the requirements of law and a schedule of the claim has been appended to the plaint by the plaintiff-Bank and the averments made therein were certified and attested by Md Monaem Hossain, Senior Principal Officer of the plaintiff-Bank by swearing affidavit. Md Monaem Hossain was examined as PW-1. In his deposition, he proved the statement of accounts which was admitted as evidence and accordingly, the Adalat was pleased to mark the same as Exhibit-12. 

21. The Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 and the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 both are special laws. In this respect, we should make clear that the Evidence Act, 1872 is a general law of evidence i.e. the provision relating to evidence as found within the four walls of the Evidence Act, 1872 under chapter 1 to 11 are General Law of Evidence. The Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 and the Commercial Documents Evidence Act, 1939 deal with Special Law of Evidence. Apart from the same, the Special Law of Evidence sporadically exists in our different legislation. The Ain, 2003 also incorporated some provisions relating to Special Law of Evidence. It is the cardinal principle of law that if there is a conflict between the general law and special law obviously, special law shall prevail. But if there is a conflict between two special laws, obviously the latest special law will get primacy over earlier one. The manner of certification of statement as mentioned in the Ain, 2003 is more stringent than that of the provision of certification as mentioned in the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891, therefore, it can safely be concluded that the certification of statement of accounts made under Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 is in addition to the Ain, 2003 not in derogation, hence, the contention of the petitioner that the statement of accounts has not been certified in view of the provision of the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 and due to non-certification of the statement of accounts (Exhibit-12) has become inadmissible as evidence is unfounded and baseless. 

22. We have perused the certified copy of the Exhibit-12. It appears that loan disbursement and repayment history has been clearly depicted therein. Admittedly, no entry was challenged by the petitioner as incorrect. The Adalat in its judgment observed: 

বাদীপক্ষে মোঃ মোনায়েম হোসেন ক্ষমতাপত্র মূলে পি/ডব্লিউ-১ হিসেবে আদালতে সাক্ষ্য প্রদান করেন । বাদী পক্ষে দাখিলী কাগজপত্র সমূহ প্রদর্শনী-১-৩, প্রদর্শনী-৪-৪ঘে), প্রদর্শনী-৫-৬, প্রদর্শনী-৭-৭ড), প্রদর্শনী-৮, প্রদর্শনী-৯-৯(ঘ), প্রদর্শনী, প্রদর্শনী-১১-১১৫খ), প্রদর্শনী-১২ এবং প্রদর্শনী-১৩-১৩৫ঘ) পর্যস্ত চিহ্নিত হয়। বিবাদী আদালতে মৌখিত এবং দালিলিক কোন সাক্ষ্য প্রদান করেননি, শুধুমাত্র পি/ডব্লিউ-১ কে জেরা করেছেন। উভয়পকেক্ষর বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবীর যুক্তিতর্ক শ্রবণ করলাম ৷ আরজি, লিখিত জবাঘ, মৌখিক এবং দালিলিক সাক্ষ্যসহ নথি পর্যালোচনা করলাম । 

23. Therefore, the argument of the petitioner that without considering the Exhibit-12, the Adalat passed the impugned judgment and decree is fallacious. 

24. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and legal position intricately involves therein, we are of the view that the Rule is devoid of any substance and hence, the Rule shall fall through. 

25. It transpires from the record that the Artha Rin Suit No. 96 of 2011 started its journey in 2011 and the plaintiff-Bank obtained decree on contest on 12-9-2013 and thereafter, the decree was put into execution. In the meantime, more than 9(nine) years have been elapsed. But due to the writ petition on flimsy ground, the decree holder-Bank could not recover the huge outstanding loan money. The actual sufferings of the decree-holders start after obtaining the decree. The petitioner-judgment-debtor took device to prolong the litigation and filed writ petition so that the decree-holder cannot enjoy the fruits of long cherished decree and, as such, the very purpose of enacting the Ain, 2003 is being frustrated which is unwanted and undesirable. 

26. As a result, the Rule is discharged, however, without passing any order as to costs. The earlier order of stay granted by this Court, thus stands vacated and recalled. 

27. The Executing Court is directed to dispose of the execution case with outmost expedition preferably within 6(six) months from the date of receiving the copy of the judgment. 

Let a copy of this judgment be communicated to the Court below at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
Md Zakir Hossain, j: At the instance of the petitioner, this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order No. 10 dated 9-4-2018 rejecting two applications one for permission to pay rest amount Taka 2,32,00,000 by installments and another for settlement conference and order No. 12 dated 10-6-2018 for publishing auction notice in the Daily Kaler Kantha and the Daily Karatoa both dated 12-6-2018 fixing .auction date to 5-7-2018 (Annexure-H & I) passed by the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Bogura (respondent No. 2) and as to why. the auction Notice published on 12-6-2018 in the daily Kaler Kantha under section 33 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 as per order dated 10-6-2018 passed in Artha Jari Case No. 165 of 2017 inviting tender from the interested persons to sell the mortgaged property mentioned in schedule of the Notice (Annexure-G) should not be declared illegal and have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. For disposal of the Rule, the short facts may be stated as follows: 
Dhaka Bank Ltd. being plaintiff filed Artha Rin Suit No. 267 of 2015 to the Artha Rin Adalat, Bogura for recovery of out-standing loan to the tune of Taka 4,04,85,429.79. Having received the summons of the said suit, the petitioner entered appearance in the Suit. Eventually, the Artha Rin Adalat, Bogura, hereinafter shortly referred to 'the Adalat', was pleased to decree the Suit as prayed for. Thereafter, the decree-holder put the decree into execution by filing Artha Jari Case No. 165 of 2017, hereinafter shortly called as 'the Execution Case'.

3. In Execution Case, the judgment-debtor filed an application on 9-4-2018 (Annexure-E) to give him installment for a period of 3 (three) years for payment of Taka 2,32,00,000 (two crore thirty two lac). On the same date, the decree-holder also filed another application (Annexure-E1) to hold settlement conference in view of section 45 of the Ain, 2003. The decree-holder filed an application for publishing notice in the daily newspaper to sell out the mortgage property on auction. 

4. Upon hearing, the Executing Court allowed the petition of the decree-holder and rejected the applications of the judgment-debtor on 9-4-2018 and accordingly, 26-4-2018 was fixed for taking step for publishing auction notice. By its order dated 10-6-2018, the Executing Court directed to float notice in the daily newspapers fixing 5-7-2018 for auction sale of the mortgage property. 

5. In the above backdrop, the petitioner being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid orders moved this Court and obtained the instant Rule. 

6. Mr Md Aktaruzzaman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the Executing Court most illegally and arbitrarily rejected the petition filed under section 49 of the Ain, 2003 for installment without assigning any good reasons and, therefore, the same is liable to be turned down by this Court. He further submits that the Adalat, without giving the opportunity to the judgment-debtor and decree-holder to exhaust the provision of section 45 of the Ain, 2003 to resolve the dispute by way of mediation, most illegally rejected the prayer for settlement conference which is illegal. 

7. He further submits that the plaint of the Artha Rin Suit has not been complied with the provision of section 6(2) of the Ain, 2003 and therefore, the judgment of the Adalat is coram non judice. 

8. He also submits that section 6(2) of the Ain, 2003 makes it abundantly clear that the requirements laid down in the section are mandatory and not obligatory in nature. The language using this section makes it clear that the plaint has to be filed along with an affidavit both as to the statement made in the plaint as well as to the document annexed to the plaint, therefore, the non compliance with the mandatory requirement of law rendered in the plaint rejected in the eye of law and consequently, the decree passed by the Adalat cannot sustain in the eye of law. 

9. As against to this, the learned Senior Counsel, Mr AM Amin Uddin along with Mr Syfuzzaman appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 3, submits that after considering materials on record, facts and circumstances of the case, the Executing Court rightly rejected the petitions by impugned order, therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

10. Mr AM Amin Uddin further submits that the Executing Court cannot go behind the decree, save few exceptions. He further submits that the application prayed for time to pay the decretal amount by installment was rightly rejected by the impugned order No. 10, dated 9-4-2018 and in the meantime, 2 years have already been elapsed but the petitioner did not pay single farthing nor contacted with the respondent Bank which amply implies that the judgment-debtor has no bonafide intention to pay off the outstanding decretal amount. 

11. He further submits that in order to prolong the execution case, the petitioner filed this writ petition as a device so that the decree-holder cannot enjoy the fruits of the long cherished decree. He further submits that the petitioner has not come with clean hands. He further submits that the petitioner has got no bonafide intention to pay the outstanding dues. Finally, he submits that without preferring appeal to the competent Court, the chastity or legality of the decree of the Adalat cannot be challenged by invoking writ jurisdiction, therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

12. Now the moot issue is—
Whether the impugned orders passed by the Executing Court are sustainable in the eye of law. 

13. We have perused the writ petition along with annexures, supplementary affidavit, affidavit-in-opposition and submissions advanced by the learned Advocates of the parties and legal position intricately involves in this Rule with great care and attention. 

14. It also appears from the record that by order No. 12 dated 10-6-2018, the Executing Court directed to publish auction notice in the Daily Kaler Kantha and the Daily Karatoa fixing 5-7-2018 for selling out the mortgage property of the judgment-debtor. 

15. It also appears from the record (Annexure-I) that the petitioner preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 88 of 2018 to the Court of District Judge, Bogura challenging the decree of the Adalat. After that, the learned District Judge called for the record. Upon considering the materials on record, the learned District Judge by its order dated 23-5-2018 rejected the appeal summarily as it has got no jurisdiction to entertain the appeal. But the decree-holder did not challenge the said order nor file any appeal to the competent Court having jurisdiction to entertain the appeal in view of section 41 of the Ain, 2003. 

16. Now we may look into the relevant provisions of mediation during pendency of the Execution Case. Section 38 of the AM, 2003 provides that during the pendency of the Execution Case, settlement of dispute may be made by mediation. Section 38 of the AM, 2003 may be read as follows: 

৩৮। জারীর পর্যায়ে মধ্যস্থতার মাধ্যমে বিনোধ নিষ্পত্তি ।--(১) এই আইনের অধীন অর্থ খণ আদালত মামলায় প্রদত্ত ডিক্রীর ধারাবাহিকতায় জারী কার্যক্রম অব্যাহত থাকার যেকোন পর্যায়ে পক্ষগণ মধ্যস্থতার মাধ্যমে জারী মামলার বিষয়বস্তু নিষ্পত্তি করিয়া আদালতকে অবহিত করিতে পারিবে ।
(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীন মধ্যস্থৃতার ক্ষেত্রে ধারা ২২ এর উপ-ধারা (২), (৩) ও (৪) এ উল্লিখিত বিধান অনুসরণ করিতে হইবে ।
(৩) আদালত, উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীন অবহিত হইলে এবং নিষ্পত্তির বিষয়ে সন্তুষ্ট হইলে, উক্ত জারী মোকদ্দমা চূড়ান্তভাবে নিষ্পত্তি করিয়া আদেশ প্রদান করিবে ।

17. Section 45 of the AM, 2003 provides that a non-obstante clause empowering the Adalat to afford the parties to resolve the dispute amicably at any stage if they wish to do the same. Section 45 may be read thus: 

৪৫ । মামলায় আপোষ নিম্পত্তি-__(১) এই আইনের কোন কিছুই বিচার কার্যক্রমের পরবর্তা যে কোন পর্যায়ে, কোন মামলার আপোষ নিষ্পত্তি করা হইতে পক্ষগণকে বারিত করিবে না।
(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীনে প্রদত্ত মামলার আপোষ নি্পত্তির সুযোগ এই আইনে মামলা নিষ্পত্তির জন্য ব্যবস্থিত অন্যান্য পদ্ধতি এবং নির্ধারিত সময়সীমার হানি বা ব্যত্যয় ঘটাইতে পারিবে না। 

18. Section 49 of the Ain, 2003 provides that when and under what circumstances the Adalat may give the judgment-debtor an opportunity -for payment of the decretal amount. For better understanding and appreciation, the same may be read as follows: 

৪৯। ঋণের কিস্তি—(১) উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে অর্থ ঋণ আদালত, বিবাদী-দায়িকের আবেদনের প্রেক্ষিতে বা স্বীয় উদ্যোগে উপযুক্ত মনে করিলে, ডিক্রীতে টাকা ১ (এক) বৎসরে ৪(চার) টি সম কি্তিতে পরিশোধের জন্য দায়িককে সুযোগ প্রদান করিতে পারিবে ।
(২) বাদী-ডিক্রীদার সম্মত থাকিলে, উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, ডিক্রীকৃত টাকা ৩€তিন) বৎসরে ১২ (বার) টি সমকিস্তিতে পরিশোধের জন্য আদালত. দায়িককে সুযোগ প্রদান করিতে পারিবে ।
(৩) উপ-ধারা 0১) বা (২) এ উল্লিখিত কোন একটি কিস্তি বকেয়া হওয়া মাত্রই সমুদয় বকেয়া তখনই পরিশোধিতব্য হইবে এবং তদ্উদ্দেশ্যে জারী কার্যক্রম যথাবিধি অনুসৃত হইবে ।

19. The judgment-debtor did not pay the outstanding dues of the decretal amount within the stipulated time fixed by the Adalat. After exhausting all the procedures as provided tinder the Ain, 2003, the Executing Court floated auction notice to sell out the mortgage property in order to satisfy the decretal amount. 

20. It is well settled principle of Apex Court that the Executing Court cannot go behind the decree, save few exceptions; if it appears to the executing court that the decree is nullity in the eye of law or the decree is passed against dead man or decree is passed by the court having no jurisdiction. 

21. It also appears from the record (annexure-C) that the petitioner filed a petition on 20-2-2018 addressing to the Manager, Dhaka Bank Ltd., Bogura Branch and thereby, he clearly promised that he would pay of the entire decretal amount within one year, but the petitioner did not pay any single amount, though in the meantime almost 2 years have been elapsed. 

22. It also appears from the record that during the hearing of the Rule, the petitioner filed an application to this court for giving the parties an opportunity to settle down their dispute amicably. Upon hearing, this Court was pleased to allow the petition and give an opportunity to the petitioner for amicable settlement with the respondent Bank and it was also directed by this court in its order dated 4-3-2020 that the parties have to inform the Court before 29-10-2010, as to whether they have been able to reach any settlement and failing which the Court will proceed it in accordance with law. But having obtained an ample opportunity, the petitioner and respondent could not settle down their dispute under section 45 of the Ain, 2003. 

23. It is true that during the pendency of the Artha Rin Suit, the Adalat has to exhaust the procedure of section 22 of the Ain, 2003 which is mandatory. But during the pendency of the Execution Proceeding, it is the absolute domain of the parties to the case to settle down their dispute amicably and accordingly, the same will be notified to the Executing Court, then it will follow the procedure as laid down under section 22 of the Ain, so far it applies. 

24. Admittedly, having obtained an ample opportunity, the parties to the Execution Case failed to mediate the dispute therefore, the submission for settlement conference is fallacious. From the aforesaid discussion, it is also crystal clear that the judgment-debtor has got no bonafide intention to pay off the outstanding decretal amount, therefore, it would not be advisable to stand against the execution proceeding. Accordingly, we hold the view that the Rule has got no merit. Consequently, the Rule shall fall through. 

25. At the time of pronouncement of the judgment, the learned Advocate of the petitioner orally apprises that he has instruction by his client not to proceed with the case. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and to prevent multiplicity of proceeding on self-same cause, we hold the view that it would be advisable to dispose of the Rule on merit. Moreover, the backdrop of the case, palpably indicates the petitioner in order to frustrate the hard-earned decree has taken different devices. We do not find any substance therein and hence, we have disposed of the Rule on merit. 

26. As a result, the Rule is discharged, however, without passing any order as to costs. The parties will bear the respective costs.

27. In appears from the record, the Artha Rin Suit and then Execution Case has been dragging for about 5 years. The main purpose of the Ain, 2003 is to dispense speedy justice but our experience shows that the borrower takes many devices to prolong the execution proceeding so that the decree holder cannot enjoy the fruits of decree. If the Execution Case is not disposed of within a reasonable time, the purpose of promulgating the Ain, 2003 will be frustrated. Therefore, the Executing Court is hereby directed to dispose of the Execution Case preferably within 06 (six) months from the date of receiving the copy of the judgment and no adjournment will be allowed from either side. 

Let a copy of the judgment be sent down to the court below at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party No 1, to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 2-2-2003 (decree signed on 9-2-2003), passed by the Additional District Judge Cum Bankruptcy Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No.633 of 1999, allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 5-9-1999 (decree signed on 15-9-1999), passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Nawabgonj, Dhaka, in Title Suit No.83 of 1997, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that the present petitioner, as plaintiff, filed Title Suit No.326 of 1993, before the 1st Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka, against the Mayor, City Corporation, Dhaka, (now the Dhaka City Corporation (North), Dhaka and 2 others. Subsequently the said suit was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 83 of 1997. The main contention of the plaintiff is that, he is the owner of the suit property and of the building mentioned in the schedule to the plaint. The further case of the plaintiff is that, he has been paying City Corporation Taxes @ Taka 120 per quarter as decided by the Review Board of the City Corporation by an order dated 17-7-1989. His further case is that, this valuation of the property is valid for the period of 5(five) years i.e. up to 1988 to 1992 and that before expiry of the said period of 5 years, from 1988-1992, the City Corporation has revised and increased the valuation. He also stated that the suit property was being used as his residence and he did not let out any portion of the said property. However, the City Corporation arranged claiming payment of tax at a higher rate and issued notice to attach of his property and he came to know that the rate of tax has been fixed @ Taka 19,340 and had been claimed with retrospective effect. It has also been stated that, he has preferred an appeal to the City Corporation, on 14-5-1992, and accordingly one Magistrate Mr Hasanur Rahmana was entrusted to enquire into the matter and, as such, the said Magistrate heard the matter on 12-10-1992 and opined that the valuation of the property can be made as per provisions of Rule 26(1)(c) of the Municipal Corporations (Taxation) Rules 1986. Thereafter, the plaintiff on 9-6-1993 came to know that the valuation of the property was fixed as per section 26(1)(c) of the Municipal Corporation (Taxation) Rules, 1986, and the valuation of the property was revised and enhanced as per provisions of Rule 26(1)(c) of the said Rules and the plaintiff was requested to pay tax of Taka 1,350 per quarter. The plaintiff further stated that the annual valuation of the suit property was made as per provisions of section 26(1)(c) and before expiry of the period of 5 years term (during 1993-94) was illegal and unlawful. His further case is that, he was not given any notice, before revising the valuation, as required by Sub-Rule (2) of Rule 26 of the said Rules. Accordingly, he has prayed for declaration that the valuation fixed on 12-7-1989 by the Review Board is lawful and that the valuation fixed on 6-9-1993 by Zone-I0 (North) of the City Corporation under Memo No. 2057/ L: B: 10 dated 9-6-1993 is illegal and ineffective in the eye of law. Hence, the suit. 

3. The defendant Nos. 1 appeared and contested in this suit by filing written statements, on 28-9-1995, denying the averments made in the plaint and further alleging their case at paragraph Nos. "Ka" to "Ta" of the written statement. The main case of the defendant is that, the quarterly tax @ Taka 120 has been increased to Taka. 1,890, from 1-9-1989, but the plaintiff did not pay the tax and Taka 19,340 has become outstanding and, therefore attachment order was sent for recovery of the outstanding dues, but the said order could not be executed because of non-co-operation of the plaintiff and the claim has been kept it in abeyance. Further case of the defendant is that the plaintiff deliberately did not pay the tax of the City Corporation. It has also been stated that as per order of the Magistrate the valuation of the property was fixed at Taka 63,000 by the City Corporation, but the Mayor on compassionate ground reduced the valuation from Taka 63,000 to Taka 45,000 with effect from 1-9-1989 and that was just and proper. It has also been stated in the written statement that the building in the suit property was two-storied building and that the plaintiff has constructed the 1st Floor from ground Floor of the building on the basis of which revaluation was indispensable and accordingly earlier valuation has been revised. It has been further stated that the plaintiff was given notice as per provision of Rule 26(2) and all formalities were followed for revaluation of the property and the City Corporation has stated that appropriate treatment has been given to the plaintiff and concession has been given in respect of the loan taken by him for the house building purpose. Accordingly, it has prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

4. The plaintiff has examined 3 witnesses, namely PWs 1-3, while he has also produced and proved certain documents, marked as exhibits 1- 17(Ka), in support of his case. On the other hand, the defendant No.1 has produced one witness, namely Md Abul Kalam Aziz who has testified as DW 1 to support the case, while the defendant has produced and proved some documents, marked as Exhibit "Ka" and "Ja". 

5. The trial court, after hearing the parties and having assessed the evidence on record, had decreed the suit, vide its judgment and decree dated 5-9-1999 (decree signed on 15-9-1999). 

6. Against the said judgment and decree of the trial court, the defendant No. 1 (City. Corporation) preferred Title Appeal No.633 of 1999, before the District Judge, Dhaka, which was heard by the Additional District Judge Cum Bankruptcy Court, Dhaka. The appellate court, after hearing the parties and having considered the evidence on record, has allowed the appeal and thereby set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial court, vide it's judgment and decree dated 2-2-2003 (decree signed on 9-2-2003). 7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree of the appellate court, the plaintiff-respondent, as the petitioner, has filed this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and obtained the present Rule. 

8. Learned Advocate Mr AU Ahmed has appeared on behalf of the petitioner. He, having placed the revisional application and other materials on record, mainly submits that, the City Corporation has revised and enhanced the valuation before expiry of the tenure of 5 years term i.e. before expiry of the fiscal years 1993-94. Therefore, the revaluation of the valuation, made on 12-7-1989, before expiry of the fiscal year 1993-94 was done in violation of the City Corporation Rules. His further contention is that no notice was served upon the plaintiff-petitioner, as required by Rule 26, for amendment of the valuation, therefore, on this ground the valuation made and the tax demanded was illegal and ineffective in the eyes of law. He also submits that, the trial court rightly assessed the evidence on record and has rightly decreed the suit. But, the appellate court has failed to appreciate the factual and legal aspects of the case and thereby it has committed grave error of law in passing the impugned judgment and decree that has resulted in error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. On a query made from the Bench the learned Advocate submits that, the statutory notice required to be issued under section 163 of the Dhaka City Corporation Ordinance, 1983, was not mandatory and was not applicable in this case. He prays for making the Rule absolute and to uphold the judgment and decree passed by the trial court by setting aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court. 

9. On the contrary, Mr Md Abdul Halim Shikder, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellant-opposite party No. 1, submits that, all the formalities required by the Rules have been complied with and there was a one-storied building in the suit premises and, during the concerned tenure, the plaintiff had raised it at 2 (two)-storied building. Accordingly, revaluation of the said property was essential and the Corporation was authorized to revise the valuation, as per law. He next submits that the revaluation was done after issuing prior notice dated 8-10-1989, as per Sub-Rule (2) of Rule 26 of the Municipal Corporation (Taxation) Rules, 1986 and the said notice was received by the plaintiff's mother. He proceeds on that, it was evident before the trial court that, the City Corporation has complied with all formalities for revising the annual valuation of the property and the statutory notice as required by section 163 was not served. Hence, the suit was not maintainable. Considering all these relevant aspects and the act and circumstances, the appellate court has rightly allowed the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court. He, therefore, prays for discharging the Rule. 

10. I have heard the learned Advocates for both the parties, perused the impugned judgments as well as pleadings of the parties, the evidences and other materials on record. 

11. The cases of the parties have been narrated above, hence, need not be repeated here. 

12. I find that, admittedly the plaintiff is the owner of the suit property situated in the schedule to the plaint. It is also admitted that, the Review Board of the City Corporation, by it's order dated 12-7-1989, has fixed the annual valuation and quarterly tax at the rate of Taka 120. 

13. The plaintiff has claimed that this valuation was valid for the term of 5 years i.e. up to financial year 1993-94. 

14. Rule 21 of the Municipal Corporation (Taxation) Rules, 1986, reads as follows:—
"Preparation of valuation list: A new valuation list shall, unless otherwise ordered by the Government, be prepared in the manner specified in rule 20 once in every five years." 

15. Hence, the valuation of the property done for the purpose of assessing and realization of the City Corporation tax is valid for a period of 5(five) years, subject, however, to the provisions of Rule 26(1) of the Municipal Corporation (Taxation) Rules, 1986 (the Taxation Rules).

16. Sub-rule (1) of Rule 26 of the Municipal Corporation (Taxation) Rules, 1986, permits the City Corporation to alter or amend the valuation of a building, the valuation of which has been increased by addition or alteration. 

17. In order to exercise the power vested by sub-rule (1) of Rule 26 of the said Rules, the City Corporation is under a mandatory legal duty, as required by sub-Rule (2) of Rule 26, to issue notice upon the owner of the building before amendment or alteration of the assessment of the valuation. Alongside, sub-Rule (3) of the Rule 26 provides that, any person aggrieved by a notice issued under sub-Rule (2) may apply to the City Corporation within 30 days as authorized by Rule 7 of the said Rules and that will be considered by an assessment of Review Board to be constituted by the City Corporation in accordance with Sub-Rule (3) of Rule 7 of the Municipal Corporation (Taxation) Rules, 1986. 

18. Besides, as per Sub-Rule (13) of Rule 7 of the said Rules, any person may prefer an appeal to the Divisional Commissioner, within 60 (sixty) days of the assessment made by the Review Board. The appeal is required to be disposed of within 120 working days from the date of filing of the appeal. The decision of the Divisional Commissioner is final subject, however, to the judicial review in the appropriate cases. 

19. In the instant case, the assessment was made on 12-7-1989 and that was valid till 1993-94. However, I find that a notice dated 8-10-1989 was served upon the plaintiff as per provisions of Rule 26(2) of the Municipal Corporation (Taxation) Rules, 1986, and the said notice was received by one Hafiza Khanom, on 19-10-1989 (Exhibit Kha), who is said to be the mother of the plaintiff. It further appears from the proposal dated 9-11-1989 that, the valuation of the schedule property has been proposed at Taka 63,000. However, it has been recorded in the note sheet (Exhibit Ga) that the plaintiff was not present, although he was issued notice. 

20. A demand notice dated 28-12-1989 was issued upon the plaintiff informing him that the valuation of the suit property has been increased at Taka 63,000 (Exhibit Gha) and the said notice was received by the mother of the plaintiff on 15-1-1990. But, the plaintiff did not file any review petition, as per provisions of Rule 7 of the Municipal Corporation (Taxation) Rules, 1986 against the revaluation dated 28-12-1989, rather he has filed an appeal before the Mayor, on 1-7-1992 (Exhibit Umo), which was not the proper procedure. However, a Magistrate namely Mr Hasanur Rahman was entrusted to give decision on the basis of the said appeal. 

21. It has been admitted in the plaint, that the said Magistrate heard both the parties on several dates and gave opinion on 12-11-1992 that revaluation of the property can be made as per Pule 26(1)(C) of the Municipal Corporation (Taxation) Rules, 1986 (Exhibit Cha). 

22. Accordingly, the City Corporation made a proposal to re-fix the valuation at Taka 63,000, however, the Mayor reduce it from Taka 63,000 to Taka 45,000. Accordingly, the Corporation made a demand effect from 1-9-1989 (Exhibit Chha), vide Memo No. 2057/ W: dated 9-6-1993, which has been impugned in this suit. 

23. The plaintiff did not file any review petition, as per Rule 7 of the Taxation Rules, against the valuation made under the Memo No. 2057/ dated 9-6-1993. 

24. Although a suit for declaration is main-tainable, if the plaintiff had taken the ground that the impugned demand was made or the valuation revised was a colorable exercise of power or it was without jurisdiction or was malqfide etc. But, the present suit of the plaintiff is totally on different ground on which the Review Board was competent to give relief. 

25. Having considered the evidence on record, I find that the City Corporation has complied with all necessary formalities before issuance of the demand notice dated 9-6-1993 and the plaintiff has been treated in accordance with law, since the notice has been issued under Rule 26(1) of the said Rules and 1(one) month time has also been given to the plaintiff to submit objection, if he had any, in formation in Form-P, vide notice dated 28-12-1989 and the said notice was received on 15-1-1990. Therefore, allegation of violation of Rule 26 does not sustain. 

26. The City Corporation has given adequate opportunity the plaintiff to agitate his grievance, as evident from Exhibit "Cha". Hence, the provision of Rule 26(2) as well as the principle of natural justice has been adhered to. Therefore, the allegation that the revaluation was made without hearing the plaintiff is not proved. 

27. On the other hand, Clause (d) Sub-Rule (1) of Rule 26 of the Municipal Corporation (Taxation) Rules, 1986 authorizes the Corporation to amend or alter the valuation and to revise the tax, since, in this case, the City Corporation has proved that the plaintiff has raised his building from the ground floor to the 1st floor. Therefore, the alteration of the valuation of the building was necessary and justifiable in this case. 

28. I also find that, the appellate court has arrived at findings of facts, supporting the defendant's case, which are based on proper assessment of evidence on record and it has correctly decided the issue of law as well. I find no case of misreading or non-reading of any evidence, nor misinterpretation of any law in passing the impugned judgment and decree. Nor, the impugned judgment and decree has resulted in any error in the decision occasioning failure of justice to any party. 

29. This Rule has no merit and the same should be discharged. 

Order 
In the result, the Rule is discharged. 
The impugned judgment and decree dated 2-2-2003 (decree signed on 9-2-2003), passed by the Additional District Judge Cum Bankruptcy Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No.633 of 1999, allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 5-9-1999 (decree signed on 15-9-1999), passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Nawabgonj, Dhaka, in Title Suit No.83 of 1997, is hereby upheld. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated. 

No order as to costs. 

Let a copy of this judgment along with the Lower Court's Record be sent down to the concerned Courts at once. 

End.

parties:
Alamgir Hossain (Bulu) (Md) -------- Petitioner
vs
Artha Rin Adalat and others -------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Zakir Hossain, J: At the instance of the petitioner, the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondent Nos. 1-3 to show cause as to why the adjudication by the judgment and decree dated 4-5-2015 and 11-5-2015 of the Artha Rin Suit No. 52 of 2014, by Artha Rin Adalat, 2nd Court, Dhaka (respondent No. 1) (Annexure-G and H) upon use of the statements of accounts being marked as Exhibit No. 11 in the said Artha Rin Suit which is inadmissible in evidence according to the provision of section 2(8) of the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891, should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, this court was pleased to stay all further proceedings of Artha Jari Case No. 269 of 2015. 

3. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule are, in brief, as follows: 
Shahjalal Islami Bank Ltd., Mitford Branch, the respondent No. 3 instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 52 of 2014 before the Artha Rin Adalat, 2nd Court, Dhaka, hereinafter shortly referred to the Adalat for realization of the outstanding amount of Taka 2,36,93,393.38. Having received the summons, the defendant-petitioner entered appearance in the suit and by filing a written statement contested the same. After conclusion of the trial, the Adalat was pleased to pass a decree on contest. 

4. Challenging the legality and propriety of the judgment and decree passed by the Adalat upon considering the statement of accounts as admissible evidence, the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the Rule. 

5. Mr AKM Asiful Haque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that though an alternative remedy is available to prefer an Appeal as per the mandate of section 41 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, in short 'the Ain, 2003', by depositing 50% decretal amount of the decree passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 52 of 2014 but the Respondent No. 1, Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat flouting the mandatory provisions as laid down under section 2(8) and section 4 of the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 accepted the statement of accounts as admissible evidence, thereby, passed the impugned judgment and decree and, as such, committed an error of law causing failure of justice. He further submits that the statements of accounts admitted as evidence (Exhibit-11) did not comply with the requirements of section 2(8) and section 4 of the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891, therefore, the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat cannot stand on its leg and it is liable to be set-aside by this Court.
 
6. Finally, he submits that since the Adalat decreed the suit on the basis of inadmissible evidence, therefore, the decree is liable to be turned down, otherwise it will entail serious injury to the petitioner. 

7. As against to this, Mr Md Akhtar-uz-zaman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 3, submits that it is well settled by the Apex Court of the country that judgment and decree of the Adalat cannot be challenged by preferring writ petition. In order to fortify his submission, he relies on the decision of the case of Gazi M Towfic vs Agrani Bank and others, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6. He also submits that the petitioner deliberately avoided alternative and efficacious remedy as available in the AM, 2003, filed this writ petition which is ex facie illegal and is liable to be discharged. 

8. He further submits that the statements of accounts have been rightly admitted as evidence in view of the special rules of evidence as embodied in the Ain, 2003. 

9. Mr Wayesh-al-Haroni, the learned DAG with Mr Md Saiful Alam, the learned AAG appearing on behalf of the respondent-Bangladesh Bank, candidly submit that the writ petition is not at all maintainable as the petitioner has got alternative and efficacious remedy under section 41 of the Ain, 2003. He also submits that after considering the materials on record and evidence adduced by both the parties, the Artha Rin Adalat came to the positive finding that the respondent-plaintiff has been able to prove the case upto the hilt and being satisfied the Court passed the decree. Therefore, this Writ Court has got no jurisdiction to question the legality of the judgment. He next submits that the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 and the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 both are special law relating to the rules of evidence and if there is a conflict between the two special laws, the latest special law shall obviously prevail, hence, the contention of the learned lawyer of the petitioner is misconceived. 

10. Finally, he submits that the issue of admissibility of the statement of accounts should be addressed by this Court, in order to do away with the obscurity for the greater benefit of all concerned.

11. The pertinent issues of this case are—
i. Whether the writ petition is at all maintainable in the eye of law; 
ii. Whether the statement of accounts (Exhibit-11) marked by the Artha Rin Adalat is legally admissible as evidence. 

12. We have perused the entire materials on record, the affidavit-in-opposition, the writ petition along with the annexures and legal position involved in this case with great care and attention and seriousness as it deserves. 

13. In order to answer the issue No. 1, we should consider some ratio enunciated by the Appellate Division in different cases. 

14. In the case of Zahirul Islam vs National Bank Limited and others, reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, where it has been decided as follows: 
`The petitioner, without filing any appeal, filed an application under Article 102 of the Constitution, namely, Writ Petition No. 892 of 1991, which was dismissed summarily by a Division Bench of the High Court Division on 30-6-1991 on the ground that the petitioner has an alternative and efficacious remedy by way of appeal... The Petition is dismissed." 

15. In the case of Gazi M Towfic vs Agrani Bank and others, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6 their Lordship of the Appellate Division clearly spelt out to the effect-"...the law is now settled that since special provision for appeal has been made against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat no application under Article 102 lies against such judgment and decree...." 

16. In the case of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) vs Artha Rin Adalat and others, reported in 59 DLR (AD) 6 the Appellate Division held: 
"...there being specific remedy in the statute for filing appeal against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat in the present case the defendant not availing of the aforesaid remedy cannot maintain writ petitions...." 

17. The judgment-debtor has alternative remedy to prefer Appeal against the decree under section 41 of the Ain, 2003 but by flouting the said provision, he filed this Writ Petition which is not maintainable in the eye of law. As the petitioner did not challenge the legality and propriety of the decree in view of the aforesaid provision of the Ain, 2003, the decree has acquired finality. The law is settled now that no petition under the Article 102(2) of the constitution lies impugning the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in a case filed by Financial Institution for realization of loan amount. 

18. To answer the issue No. 2, we should go into the relevant provisions as enshrined in the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891. Section 2(8) and section 4 of the said Act may be read as follows: 
Section 2(8)—"Certified copy" means a copy of any entry in the books of a bank together with a certificate written at the foot of such copy that it is a true copy of such entry, that such entry is contained in one of the ordinary books of the bank and was made in the usual and ordinary course of business, and that such book is still in the custody of the bank, such certificate being dated and subscribed by the principal accountant or manager of the bank with his name and official title. Section 4—Subject to the provisions of this Act, a certified copy of any entry in a banker's book shall in all legal proceedings be received as prima facie evidence of the existence of such entry, and shall be admitted as evidence of the matters, transactions and accounts therein recorded in every case where, and to the same extent as, the original entry itself is now by law admissible, but not further or otherwise. 

19. In the case of Radheshyam G. Garg vs Safiyabai Ibrahim Lightwalla, reported in AIR (1988) Born. 361, it was held: "In my judgment the aforesaid view of the learned Judge of the lower appellate Court was hyper-technical. The said extract of account was duly signed by the Agent of the bank. Implicit in it was a certificate that it was a true copy of an entry contained in one of the ordinary books of the bank and was made in the usual and ordinary course of business and that such book was in the custody of the bank. The detailed ingredients mentioned in the defining Clause 8 of Section 2 of the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 for qualifying to be 'certified copy' are not mandatory but merely directory. Sufficient compliance depending upon facts and circumstances of each case is enough to qualify a document to be 'certified copy'. I, therefore, hold that the said extract of account produced at Exh. 55. A is admissible in evidence..." 

20. The Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is a special law which is clearly conceived from its preamble, objects and reasons as appended to the Draft Bill presented to the Parliament by the concerned Ministry. Section 8 of the Ain, 2003 has clearly stated that the essential ingredients to be incorporated in the plaint, as plaint is the foundation of the plaintiff's case. 

21. Section 8 of the Ain, 2003 may be read as follows-
“৮। আরজি ।-(১) আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান আরজি দাখিলের মাধ্যমে মামলা দায়ের করিবে এবং উক্ত আরজিতে, অন্যান্য বিষয়ের মধ্যে, নিম্নবর্ণিত বিষয়সমূহ উল্লিখিত হইবে, যথাঃ
(২) পূর্ববর্তী উপ-ধারায় বর্ণিত বিষয়াদির অতিরিক্ত, বাদী, আর্জিতে আরও অন্তর্ভুক্ত করিবে-
(ক) একটি তফসিল, যাহাতে প্রদর্শিত হইবে-
(অ) বিবাদীকে প্রদত্ত মূল ঋণ বা, ক্ষেত্রমত, বিনিয়োগকৃত টাকার পরিমাণ;
(আ) স্বাভাবিক সুদ বা ক্ষেত্রমত, মুনাফা বা ভাড়া হিসেবে আরোপিত টাকার পরিমাণ;
(ই) দণ্ড সুদ হিসাবে আরোপিত টাকার পরিমাণ:
(ঈ) আর অন্যান্য বিষয় বাবদ বিবাদীর উপর আরোপিত টাকার পরিমাণ;
(উ) মামলা দায়েরের পূর্ব পর্যন্ত প্রণীত শেষ হিসাব মতে বিবাদী কর্তৃক বাদী আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানকে ঋণ বা পাওনা পরিশোধ বাবদে জমাদানকৃত টাকার পরিমাণ; এবং
(ঊ) বাদী কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ও ধার্য মোট এবং বিবাদী কর্তৃক পরিশোধিত মোট টাকার তুলনামূলক অবস্থান…..”

22. The relevant provisions of sections 6(2), (3) and (4) of the Ain, 2003 may be stated for better appreciation. 
Section 6(2) of the Ain, 2003 may be read as follows-
৬। বিচার পদ্ধতি ।-(২) এই আইনের অধীন কোন মামলা আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক আরজি দাখিলের মাধ্যমে দায়ের করিতে হইবে, আরজির বক্তব্য এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট দালিলিক প্রমাণাদির সমর্থনে আরজির সহিত একটি হলফনামা (Affidavit) সংযুক্ত করিতে হইবে আরজির সহিত প্রদেয় কোর্ট ফি (ad valorem) প্রদান করিতে হইবে এবং দাখিলকৃত আরজি যথাযথ হইলে আদালতের নির্ধারিত রেজিষ্টারে উহা ক্রম অনুসারে অন্তর্ভুক্ত করিতে হইবে।
Section 6(3) of the Ain, 2003 runs as follows-
৬। বিচার পদ্ধতি ।-(৩) এই আইনের অধীন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক দায়েরকৃত মামলা বিবাদী কর্তৃক লিখিত জবাব দাখিলের মাধ্যমে প্রতিদ্বন্বিতা করা যাইবে, লিখিত জবাবের বক্তব্যের এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট দালিলিক প্রমাণাদির সমর্থনে লিখিত জবাবের সহিত একটি হলফনামা (Affidavit) সংযুক্ত করিতে হইবে এবং দাখিলকৃত লিখিত জবাব মামলার নথিতে সামিল হইবে।
Section 6(4) of the Ain, 2003 may be read as follows—
৬। বিচার পদ্ধতি ।-(8) এই আইনের অধীন অর্থ ঋণ আদালতে মামলা নিষ্পত্তির ক্ষেত্রে উপ-ধারা (২) ও (৩) এর বিধান অনুযায়ী সংযুক্ত হলফনামা (Affidavit) মৌলিক সাক্ষ্য (Substantive evidence) হিসাবে গণ্য হইবে, এবং আদালত কোন মামলার একতরফা বা তাৎক্ষণিক নিষ্পত্তির ক্ষেত্রে কোন সাক্ষীকে পরীক্ষা ব্যতিরেকে, কেবল এইরূপ হলফনামা-যুক্ত আরজি বা লিখিত জবাব ও সংশ্লিষ্ট দালিলিক প্রমাণাদি বিশ্লেষণ করিয়া রায় বা আদেশ প্রদান করিবে। 

23. Section 6(4) clearly spelt out that the affidavit filed by the petitioner along with the plaint and written statement shall be treated as substantive evidence and even without taking evidence, the court may pronounce its judgment on perusal of the plaint and written statement. On plain reading of the plaint, it transpires that the plaint was filed fulfilling the requirements of law and a schedule of the claim has been appended to the plaint by the plaintiff-Bank and the averments made therein were certified and attested by Md Masud Alam, Senior Officer of the plaintiff-Bank by swearing affidavit. Md Masud Alam was examined as P.W-1. In his deposition, he proved the statement of accounts which was admitted as evidence and accordingly, the Adalat was pleased to mark the same as Exhibit-11. The petitioner having obtained ample opportunity did not challenge the evidence of PW-1. The Exhibit-11 was admitted as evidence without any objection from the side of defendant-petitioner. 

24. The Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 and the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 both are special laws. In this respect, we should make clear that the Evidence Act, 1872 is a general law of evidence i.e. the provision relating to evidence as found within the four walls of the Evidence Act, 1872 under chapter 1 to 11 are General Law of Evidence. The Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 and the Commercial Documents Evidence Act, 1939 deal with Special Law of Evidence. Apart from the same, the Special Law of Evidence sporadically exists in our different legislations. The Ain, 2003 also incorporated some provisions relating to Special Law of Evidence. It is the cardinal principle of law that if there is a conflict between the general law and special law obviously, special law shall prevail. But if there is a conflict between two special laws, obviously, the latest special law will get primacy over earlier one. The manner of certification of statement as mentioned in the Ain, 2003 is more stringent than that of the provision of certification as mentioned in the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891, therefore, it can safely be concluded that the certification of statement of accounts made under Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 is in addition to the Ain, 2003 not in derogation, hence, the contention of the petitioner that the statement of accounts has not been certified in view of the provision of the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 and due to non-certification of the statement of accounts (Exhibit-11) has become inadmissible as evidence is unfounded and baseless. 

25. We have perused the certified copy of the Exhibit-11. It appears that loan disbursement and repayment history has been clearly depicted therein. Admittedly, no entry was challenged by the petitioner as incorrect. 

26. On perusal of the materials on record and evidence of PW-1, the Adalat came to the findings: “বাদী সাক্ষী PW-1 এর মৌখিক সাক্ষ্য পর্যালোচনায় এবং বাদী ব্যাংক কর্তৃক দাখিলীয় ব্যাংক হিসাব বিবরণী (প্রদর্শনী-১১১ সহ প্রদর্শনী আকারে দাখিলীয় অন্যান্য সকল কাগজাদি পর্যালোচনায় বাদীর দাবীকৃত টাকা বিবাদীগণের নিকট পাওনা রয়েছে মর্মে সিদ্ধান্ত গৃহীত হলো।”

27. Therefore, the argument of the peti-tioner that the decree passed considering inadmissible evidence (Exhibit 11) is illegal, cannot be accepted. 

28. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and legal position intricately involved therein, we are of the view that the Rule is devoid of any substance and hence, the Rule shall fall through. 

29. It transpires from the record that the Artha Rin Suit No. 52 started its journey in 2014 and the plaintiff-Bank obtained decree on 4-5-2015 and thereafter, the decree was put into execution. In the meantime, more than 7(seven) years have been elapsed. But due to the writ petition on a flimsy ground, the decree holder-Bank could not recover the huge outstanding loan money. The actual sufferings of the decree-holders start after obtaining the decree. The petitioner-judgment-debtor took device to prolong the litigation and filed writ petition so that the decree-holder cannot enjoy the fruits of long cherished decree and, as such, the very purpose of enacting the Ain, 2003 is being frustrated which is unwanted and undesirable. 

30. As a result, the Rule is discharged, however, without passing any order as to costs. The earlier order of stay granted by this Court, thus stands vacated and recalled. 

31. The Executing Court is directed to dispose of the execution case with outmost expedition preferably within 6(six) months from the date of receiving the copy of the judgment. 

Let a copy of this judgment be communicated to the Court below at once. 

End.
